A breach should be expected, and encryption is the most effective way to mitigate its cost.
Data remains encrypted in transit, in memory, and in database storage.
While the data is encrypted, it can be searched and fetched to the application, and only there is it decrypted.
The key is never revealed.
No application changes are required.
Established schemes such as AES are combined with oblivious RAM and differential privacy to index encrypted records efficiently and securely.
The route to market is direct engagements with financial services and medium-sized cloud-native companies, plus database providers as channel partners.
Male fertility has halved, infertility is common, male factors account for much of it, and sperm quality declines as men age.
Going to a clinic to test and freeze sperm is an awkward, clinical experience.
A home kit's buffering medium keeps a deposit viable for up to 48 hours so the kit can be picked up and sent to a partner clinic to be tested, analyzed, and frozen.
Clients receive a personalized fertility report with an overall assessment, recommendations, and core measures such as concentration, volume, morphology, and motility.
A post-thaw motility check the day after freezing confirms the sample is still viable for future use.
Analysis and freezing are offered both as a bundle and unbundled, with analysis first and an option to freeze later.
The product is priced at 10% of the $10,000 cost of egg freezing.
Companies that already offer fertility benefits are a target client for the service.
Direct-to-consumer sales target men in high-stress professional jobs who may want a family later.
Indirect outreach targets men's partners, who often make the household's medical decisions.
City data sits in legacy silos, spreadsheets, and paper, and manual aggregation is slow and costly.
The platform is modular and aligned with city services from childcare to fire departments to infrastructure.
The childcare module lets city leaders track performance, optimize costs, and forecast demand over the coming years.
A standalone data bridge installed on the client server connects to legacy databases and runs queries daily.
Records that exist only on paper are digitized as a service.
The product covers European localization requirements that US GovTech startups do not meet.
The business is software-as-a-service with a one-time setup fee tied to the number of database integrations and an annual license tied to modules and city size.
Sales are made on-site by regionally distributed teams.
Scaling also uses political networks and social proof.
The company starts in Germany and then scales to other European markets.
Living with diabetes is difficult because food, activity, medication, stress, and weather affect blood sugar, and existing apps only give tools for manually logging and analyzing those details.
Spike automatically collects details about life, routine, activity, and vitals and proactively provides insulin tips, reminders, and food suggestions.
Guardians and doctors are informed in real time and alerted if an unusual pattern is detected.
Spike is free forever for diabetics, and insurance companies, self-insured employers, and others who want to enhance productivity pay for it.
African logistics has no flexibility or centralized coordination, so shippers cannot reliably get trucks and truckers sit idle.
The platform coordinates a journey by redirecting trucks when loading fails and by making decisions from data collected on every truck and trip.
Cargo owners can see where their trucks are live at any stage through dashboards and tracking.

Buying sexual wellness products is a poor experience for women because most products are designed by men, education is scarce, in-store and online shopping are intimidating or hypersexualized, and women are shamed for enjoying sex.
Unbound designs next-generation sexual wellness products at half the price.
Most vibrators contain carcinogens because they are not regulated by the FDA, so the line has to be body-safe.
Educational content guides a woman to the right product.
Palma is a discreet wearable vibrating ring that closes the orgasm gap and lets the user personalize the vibration pattern with a patent-pending accelerometer.
A direct-to-consumer model lets a woman shop from home and cuts out distributors who take 40% of the margin.
Cooking with charcoal, firewood, or kerosene causes indoor air pollution that leads to heart disease, chronic lung cancer, miscarriage, sudden infant death, and pneumonia in young children.
The clean cookstove is affordable and smokeless, cooks five times faster than a traditional stove, and self-generates 50 watts that can charge phones, power banks, televisions, and radios.
Biomass pellets processed from agricultural, household, and commercial waste are 80% cheaper than charcoal, burn without smoke, and cook twice as fast as a traditional combustible stove.
The products are sold through existing cooperative societies and microfinance institutions.
Local vendors who sell kerosene, firewood, or charcoal can sell the products at a better margin without being pushed out of their market.
After-sale support backs a 12-month guarantee when something goes wrong.
Multimodal freight data is fragmented because providers rely on legacy systems that produce unreliable information, so shippers cannot tell where goods are or when they will arrive.
Provider information is paired with satellite tracking of ships and planes and with trucks' GPS and IoT devices.
Data science predicts arrival times from external factors such as traffic and events and sends alerts to operational teams on their smartphones.
Flyers are otherwise treated like cattle in commercial planes or pay 5,000 euros for private aviation.
A passenger can request a flight that is not already posted, and that request is sent to private pilots in the region.
A tailor-made insurance product gives customers an extra 1 million euro of coverage on each flight.
The platform takes a commission of 15% plus 4 euro on each shared-flight transaction.

Existing social media exposes children to predatory algorithms, addictive loops, strangers, compromised data, and inappropriate content, and children lie about their age to get onto platforms that are not made for them.
Kid-friendly creator tools let children make and share expressive videos, and creating together with friends, siblings, or parents deepens both the skills and the relationships.
Children connect through guided profiles and are steered toward socially and emotionally appropriate communication, with trolls appearing only as part of the curriculum.
Parents can turn tools on and off for a child's age, stage, and preferences, and a guided curriculum decides when new tools are introduced.
Adults trained in developmental psychology curate and moderate the feed so the content is appropriate for children, and the feed includes pauses to reflect on how social media is being used.
Verified parental consent keeps the platform privacy-compliant around the world.
An invitation system will let children connect with friends once the social features are available.
Brands that market to children lack a way to engage them, and spaces for reaching parents are crowded, so growth runs through parents and brand partnerships.
Electrical lighting produces large carbon emissions, consumes about 15% of global electricity, and exposes most people to light pollution.
A growing, living bioluminescent material can reduce environmental impact, improve wellness through the quality of natural light, and open new designs.
Glow Event is ephemeral light for temporary spaces and can glow for up to one week.
Pipelight is a maintained bioreactor that continuously grows microbes, can be fed with industrial waste, and yields ongoing light plus organic byproducts.
Energy providers license the technology and operate the lighting systems.
Blockchain is difficult to use because people must access many networks and securely manage their own credentials.
There is almost no interoperability between blockchains, so assets such as Bitcoin and Ethereum cannot be traded easily across systems.
A human value address replaces a blockchain address with a username that is used for the user's transactions.
The blockchain communications protocol lets users transact across blockchains, including an atomic swap between two chains.
Enterprise licenses for the protocol are sold through partnerships with large companies and blockchain payment processors.
The technology is free for non-commercial use by private developers so that group will adopt it.
Millions of travel sources and services make smooth planning impossible, leaving people with irrelevant content and too many options.
From the travelers' combined interests, the platform generates an itinerary that orders spots by the best transport and matches a recommended stay for each overnight stop.
The service makes money through brand and affiliate partnerships with travel brands.
Aviation agreed to net-zero emissions by 2050, but the current trajectory still produces about three gigatons of CO2-equivalent a year in 2050.

Hydrogen is the energy path because it is good enough on both well-to-flight energy efficiency and aircraft range, speed, and payload, while batteries miss aircraft performance and sustainable aviation fuel misses energy efficiency.

A scalable powertrain supplies hydrogen tanks, a fuel cell, an air supply, batteries, and two electric motors, with the tanks integrated below the cabin and thermal management built into the aircraft.
The first aircraft is a pressurized business jet for six to eight passengers that flies at the speed and range of existing aircraft and matches existing missions.
European airports have to be ready to supply hydrogen, and traffic is concentrated so that 200 airports handle about 80 percent of it.
Obtaining cattle weight is labor-intensive, time-consuming, and expensive, so it is rarely done, and weighing the cow is stressful, can injure the animal, and makes it lose weight.

Portable 3D-camera software estimates cattle weight frequently, without stress, and about ten times faster than a scale, so farmers know when to sell, change feed, treat sick cows, dose medicine, and choose genetics.
The platform recommends products that can improve weight gain and earns a commission on those products.

Natural disasters and wars require rebuilding, and a typical single-story house takes at least three months, which is expensive, time-consuming, labor-intensive, and unsafe, so a family has no shelter for that period.
The 3D printer is designed to build single-story houses in one week, reducing total construction time by up to 75%, with cost savings and safer construction.
The concrete mix is two times stronger than traditional mixes, sets 20 times faster, is flowable enough to pass through the printer, bonds layers instantly, and is environmentally friendly.
Professionals who bill by the hour forget mobile calls taken outside the workday, and about 40 percent of that phone time goes unbilled because capturing it is too time-consuming.
A third button on the mobile call screen starts automatic tracking of that call for billing.
About 1.4 billion tons of food are wasted every year, much of it before anyone touches it, and a rising population faces a massive lack of food, especially protein.

An edible insect is raised in a hatchery for egg production, then eggs and ground food waste go into an incubator that speeds growth and decomposition, and the output is separated into market-ready fertilizer and dried insect protein powder.
Companies pay the venture to take their food waste, and the venture also sells insect-based protein powder and fertilizer.
The production system is exponentially more efficient than other protein sources, needing minimal water and land, zero grain, and almost zero carbon emissions.
The same protein sources can be used for pets and humans, and low regulation makes a first product for reptiles, fish, and birds easy to bring to market.
Edible insects became legal in Europe.
No FDA approval is needed, so the protein supplement market is an easy place to start.
The first human customers are athletes who already add whey protein, renal and cancer patients who cannot digest regular meat, and people who are allergic to meat and cannot consume dairy.
The species produced is approved as edible by the FAO.

A winning strategy has to be rebuilt every day from all the news, each company's prices, and corporate fundamentals, and even with a stack the work is coding-heavy, expensive, inefficient, and time-consuming.
The platform offers several ready-to-use trading strategies that are three years back-tested, powered by AI, and deployable on a third-party broker in a few clicks.
A second layer of forward or live testing lets people validate performance with automated paper trading, using real markets but fake money, before they risk cash.
Every user gets a free trial, then pays by the number of backtests, forecasts, and automated traders, averaging $400 per user per year.

Traditional farming on arid land is inefficient in resource use and quality; in the GCC most freshwater produces little of the food supply, and consumers are left with low-quality seasonal local produce or extremely expensive air-freighted imports.
The venture designs, builds, and operates high-tech greenhouses.
An IoT-enabled triple-play climate system uses mechanical, evaporative, and high-pressure fogging cooling, all controlled from one brain.
When a pest gets in, beneficial insects attack and eliminate it, so the plants are protected by nature rather than by chemicals.
Sales go direct to retailers and wholesalers, cutting a typical five-step distribution channel down to two steps.

People spend on average 17 hours looking for a car because a great deal saves money, and in MENA there is no centralized platform, information is inconsistent and illegitimate, and pricing is not standardized.
A shopper can photograph a car on the street to identify it and see estimated value and expected depreciation, while the pricing AI scans the market and constantly adjusts.
A search immediately shows all cars on all websites in the country and surfaces the best deals.
An AI negotiation chatbot contacts every dealer and negotiates so final prices are ready when the shopper searches.
A WhatsApp integration lets the shopper contact the seller and book a test drive.
OEMs and certified dealers are sent leads on their featured new and used cars.
Brands get a business-intelligence tool showing the current market ecosystem, brand loyalty, and car retail inventory.
The app shows leasing options for cars as well as new and used cars for sale.

A student who needs a tutor tomorrow may find private centers closed or face an hour's commute, and about one in three students spends four to five hours finding someone qualified, accessible, and available.
The app is a peer-to-peer platform where a student picks a course, selects a pre-vetted tutor based on preferences, and books a session directly.
An algorithm favors tutors by proximity, educational background, and hours tutored, and a graph of students, tutors, and their interactions shows personalized recommendations in real time.
Tutor hiring is automated: applicants submit documents and interviews, and machine learning helps the HR team pre-select candidates.

Once a session is done, the student receives a progress report.

Institutions, universities, and schools will be charged $1,000 per month for analytics on their students' tutoring activities.
Patents are registered for this protection technology.

Under a revenue-sharing model, the venture develops the automotive security, an OEM deploys it in vehicles, and an insurer, wireless carrier, or traditional security company provides the subscription to the fleet owner.
Scaling into the market requires integrating the software with automotive hardware.
A person can have a concussion with no signs or symptoms, returning to play would be harmful, and in most of these cases the person would have gone back in.
A statistical computer-vision algorithm reads the iris response to a light stimulus, and a neural network classifies whether the person has head trauma.
The system is HIPAA compliant.
The subscription includes a dashboard and data-management system so an institution can track players' health.
The machine 3D-prints a mold, injects it with off-the-shelf manufacturing materials, the mold is dissolved, and a metal part is centered in a furnace.

Small and retail businesses suffer frequent robberies, most of them unsolved, because cameras are passive and human remote monitoring is too expensive, so help is usually called only after the robber is gone.
An analyst is alerted by the AI within fractions of a second, decides the response, and police are contacted while the crime is happening rather than after.
False positives are kept and used for retraining, so the platform gets smarter and produces fewer false positives.
Deep learning lets analysts who could watch 15 to 20 camera streams monitor 500 or more feeds.
Traditional human-only remote video monitoring is ten times more expensive than the platform.

Machines now need large volumes of structured training data, but most data is unstructured, data scientists spend most of their time cleaning it, and few companies address that problem at enterprise scale.
Fetal malformations are often misdiagnosed because ultrasound operators miss required views and many exams are incomplete.
The service is a vendor-agnostic cloud product that connects to any ultrasound machine through a standard API.
The software checks that the exam captured the required anatomical views and tells the operator which regions were missed.
Guided diagnostics localizes a fetal malformation and alerts the obstetrician so the finding is not missed.
Data taken from the exam automates the reporting and documentation that would otherwise be written by hand.
Hospitals pay a baseline subscription plus a volume charge for calls to the algorithms.

Property managers lack the tools to judge whether residents will pay, so rent is due on the first, late fees hit by the third, eviction follows by the fifth, and move-in requires a certified lump sum covering first month, last month, and deposit.
Owner-operators need a payment ecosystem that is fully online and integrated into accounting so they can see what is due and reduce pay risk.
Residents can schedule online certified payments that the owner-operator can treat as guaranteed when the funds hit the bank.

Point-of-sale installment financing lets residents spread move-in and tight-month rent over time while the owner is paid up front, using rent history and bank access to issue only one loan at a time within seconds.
The product is free to property owners, is distributed through management groups running roughly 50 to 500 properties, and earns revenue from loan origination and payment processing fees.
Credit is broken for most Americans: many scores are subprime, people are afraid to check them, most reports contain errors, and the cost of bad credit can block the home or job they want.

A guided process captures how users feel about credit and what they want, diagnoses the score, links the credit report, prescribes how to resolve questionable items, and then uses behavioral economics to set concrete actions that raise the score.
The company makes money by matching users who have improved their credit to financial products and referring them.
The company will then build its own innovative and flexible financial products for those users.

A data fabric connects important data across silos, holds business logic, adapts in real time when the data or model changes, links that data instantly without changing existing applications or writing code, and lets users build applications that reach insight.
Most people do not know which skincare products they are buying or putting on their face, and many cosmetic ingredients are harsh chemicals that can make skin worse.

A phone-based consultant powered by human expertise and artificial intelligence profiles the shopper with questions and a photo, places them among more than 30 skin types, recommends a product from that profile and from similar people, and has a human advisor validate and narrow the result to one product the shopper can buy.
Existing connectivity protocols have limited range and connectivity and are often restricted by hardware, so everyday access still depends on key fobs, phone pairing, and paper tickets.

Silent audio just above human hearing carries data between devices, including locally while offline, for identification and authentication and across phones, broadcasts, tickets, point-of-sale systems, and cars.
Data over audio is sold as a service priced per device per year.
People already communicate with images, but logos in mobile messaging cannot do much, and finding or sharing information while texting means leaving the conversation to search across other apps.
Deep-linked logos inside messaging aggregate actionable information across services for places and people, and anyone can add a logo profile or generate one instantly through Google.
Brands can use their logo for premium placement, branded content, customizations, app-to-app integrations, and analytics so the customer experience extends into messaging.
Most companies use third-party data, and the growth in sources, formats, and access frequency makes managing data between companies technically and operationally hard.

Aspiring artists either cannot access quality producers or cannot afford a music career, and producers lack relationships with artists who will buy their beats.

Service professionals face lease-geography limits on where they can work and operational stress from high renter turnover.

Keyword search and prestige markers such as well-known schools and employers miss high-potential candidates and surface false positives.
Computer vision and natural language processing extract each resume into a structured profile.

A one-line widget on the employer's site captures applications by simplifying the apply step.

About a third of clothing is returned because design uses two body shapes out of nine, so fit is a shape problem and not only a size problem.

Most people with a mental health condition get no care, and large existing spending still misses those at the highest risk.
Anonymous therapist-moderated groups of five to seven combine always-available text peer support with scheduled voice therapy.
Language models flag suicidal or malicious messages, including latent wording and conversational context, so providers step in only when a message needs them.

A see-through device projects the patient's anatomy onto the surgeon's retina in real time, with surgical precision and depth perception.

Most people have a smartphone, but a majority of the population has no internet access.

A buyer who puts one unit in the kitchen will want more for other rooms and the office.

Crowdsourced maternal and fetal data powers cloud machine learning that helps doctors predict and manage complications earlier.
The venture addresses traffic and air pollution, and scooters in Asia that are low quality, out of fashion, and short of take.

A customization system, made possible with additive manufacturing, lets buyers choose the steering, color, and components, which is otherwise costly.

Commercial construction sites are unpredictable and exposed to burst-pipe leaks, mold that can grow within 48 hours and force costly rework, and fire, and most sites have no active fire monitoring.

A site deployment digests the floor plan, places sensors through a risk audit, and brings the system live at those locations.

Moving money in Africa is difficult because transaction costs are about 15 times higher and settlement can take up to 20 days.
More than 155 mobile-money wallets run isolated from one another, which makes cross-network, cross-border, and online payments difficult.

Airtime can be topped up to any prepared mobile phone in Africa across 42 countries.

Multi-channel selling is tedious, time-consuming, and hard to manage in real time because merchants must switch platforms and replicate listings, orders, and inventory without central management.
Automated real-time inventory synchronization imports orders and updates stock on other channels, preventing stockouts and overselling.

Viewers can stream the service on a mobile phone app and on TV.

Software on everyday devices can take on heavy jobs such as video encoding, generative AI, and 3D rendering.

Millions of remote fans are disconnected from the stadium, while broadcast brings the game from the stadium out to fans around the world.

Sponsors get a brand-integration context by carrying cheers from around the world into memorable moments.

A crowd-sourced social map helps fans find tailgates, parking, food, beer, and friends in a crowd.
A live geofence chat lets nearby fans share photos, video, and information with each other.

Evaluating one protein takes expert know-how and analysis of large, scattered data, an average biotech must evaluate about 25,000 proteins, and subjective manual filters leave the best targets out.

Historical personalization based on likes, cohorts, segments, and A/B tests does not target a person at the current moment.

Large-audience video delivered through a content delivery network introduces about one to two minutes of latency.

Freelance editors can log into a client's studio remotely and create the needed video within a few days.
Clients can search footage by sentiment, object recognition, and transcription.
The offering is sold as a subscription.

Parents of school-going children face five major pain points: communication gaps with schools and teachers, child safety, security and health, instant progress and behaviour reports, having to be present to pay fees, and daily needs such as uniforms and stationery.
The app gives parents and teachers two-way notifications and communication.
Parents receive report cards instantly through the app.
GPS tracking is used to monitor the child's security.

Uniforms and stationery can be bought in the app and delivered home.

People spend over 90% of their time indoors, where unseen pollutants and exhaled carbon dioxide commonly reach about three times outdoor levels and cognitive performance falls sharply.

A microfluidic photobioreactor uses LED-lit biochips of photosynthetic algae to absorb carbon dioxide and produce oxygen more efficiently than trees.

Under-sink systems take hours to install and return about one gallon of water for every four gallons put in.

A smartphone on Wi-Fi can control the purifier, show the TDS level, and share it.
Water from the purifier costs about $0.03, presented as about twenty times better than typical bottled brands.

Machine-learning algorithms detect issues such as cyberbullying, sexting, depression, or suicide and alert the parent with recommended actions, without giving the parent open access to the child's messages.

Schools and nonprofits receive affiliate revenue for offering the service to families, which supports fundraising and student safety.

Hospital partnerships supply medical images used to train the algorithms.
The software is in a three-phase FDA process that the company describes as a clearance rather than an approval.

Comparing a full crawl of the site with the pages Google discovered shows which content was ignored, why, what to change, and whether the results moved.
The product is available to businesses as a monthly SaaS subscription.
Home devices are easy to hack because their makers lack security practice, and once an intruder is on the network they can reach the household's other devices and personal data.
A network gateway sends metadata to the cloud, where threat intelligence and machine-learning models of device behavior block only the abnormal activity and leave the device working.
The device sells for $99 plus an $8.99 monthly fee that keeps every device on the network protected.
Encryption makes data unsearchable and unusable, so a software team's core functions become impossible and the enterprise must choose between convenience and security.
Searchable encryption can search encrypted data as easily and quickly as Google searches the web, without revealing the key, and the search is built on AES-256.
Git Zero is encrypted Git hosting that encrypts source code and still allows search while the code remains encrypted.
The brain can be stimulated non-invasively, without surgery, by transcranial direct current stimulation.
Priming the motor cortex before training makes it more plastic, so athletes get more out of that training in strength and skill.

The headset technology is defensible, with 27 patents filed.
Halo makes money by selling headsets and semi-disposable primers and earpads.
Stand-up comedy is a top interest for a very large audience.
Streaming has not caught up with comedy, so only about 10 percent of comedy is available and only 1 percent of the market.
The app is a streaming service built from the ground up for comedy and spoken word.
Spoken-word technology transcribes every joke, which powers a profanity filter and radio stations based on the subject of the joke.
Listening is ad-supported, and $7.99 a month adds ad-free listening, offline play, and exclusive content.
Comedians share revenue on every stream and promote the app.
The company is a primary distribution arm for top record labels.

Current high-visibility clothing, retro-reflectives, and tail lights are limited, often invisible from outside angles, and look like a traffic cone, while cyclists and pedestrians are being killed on the road.
The garments combine lighting hardware and software that turn harvested data into visual cues, messages, and notifications.
The company sells its own smart apparel for running, biking, and motorcycling, including through college bookstores.
Licensing lets other brands take the lighting into further consumer, industrial, and enterprise uses.
Candidates and employers hire on the wrong data: most jobs are never advertised, and turnover comes from soft-skill mismatch while resumes show only hard skills.
Cognitive assessments predict job performance better than interviews, experience, or education, but they are long, expensive, and slow, so almost no one uses them.
Twenty-minute mobile games measure soft skills, and a model of a team's top performer finds other people likely to perform like that person while ignoring signals such as gender, education, and race.
Companies pay a one-time setup fee to build the top-performer model and a subscription to filter inbound candidates against it.
Companies can pay a sourcing fee for undiscovered talent already on the platform.
Anyone can download the games for free and play them to learn their own talents.

The underwater robot is intuitive to pilot, easy to maintain, and costs a fraction of existing inspection solutions.
One upload sends the inspection to a cloud service where the farm manager can see the whole farm and file the report in one click.
Good coffee is hard to make at home, and single-serve pods are wasteful, expensive, and not fresh.
Centrifugal force brews coffee the way baristas and roasters want, without pods, filters, or other wasteful materials.
The centrifugal brewing technology is patented.
When beans run low, a sensor orders fresh beans from local roasters through the app, and the roaster ships them.
The company manufactures the machine and makes margins on machine sales.
The company takes a cut of every bean order that goes through the roaster marketplace.
Digital tools under $5,000 still cannot cut hard, flat materials, so those parts are made by hand.
Wazer is a desktop waterjet that cuts any material from a digital design, more accurately than by hand, and is compact, clean, safe, and quiet, for under $4,000.
Four patents are pending on the waterjet redesign.
Relapse is driven by lack of communication and lack of accountability for recovery activities.
Geolocation and accelerometers verify that a person attended a recovery activity for the whole time, and a check-in from the wrong place is rejected.
The support network can see progress, receives alerts when the recovery program is skipped, and gets a message to reach out when the person is isolating.
Points earned in recovery can be redeemed for rewards such as fitness classes, yoga, and coffee that do not trigger technology addiction.
Inpatient treatment centers are the first sales channel and use the platform's data for referrals, outcomes, and studies.

Farms depend on heavily regulated H2A seasonal labor and must track work down to a person and a place, but most still use pen and paper and Department of Labor audits often find violations.

The software calculates hourly pay and piece-rate pay and applies the higher amount farms are required to pay, so payroll stays accurate and compliant.
A site can recommend only from actions on its own website or app, and without a time context it cannot tell a gift bought weeks ago from the shopper's own current plans.

Technology can replace most of a hospital's administrative layer, including registration, billing, and shared records, with a platform that connects patients and doctors rather than a building.
A patient can onboard by scanning an insurance card so the carrier supplies the information, without a long registration form.
The phone holds a snapshot of health organized by condition, including medical images, lab results, referrals, and appointments.
A prescription can be sent to a pharmacy for pickup or delivered to the patient's house, and the app can turn on pill reminders from the drug's schedule.
A patient can find a specialist and send the referral from the app.
Each case keeps the message history with the doctor and the chart the doctors use, and the doctor experience is designed along with the patient experience.

A patient can request help, answer questions that adapt to their history, and have a physician give a home treatment plan or ask them to schedule a clinic exam, with virtual and in-person context carried both ways.
Controlling the physician applications, the patient applications, and third-party integrations is what makes an experience traditional providers cannot design.
The platform will be available to independent practices across the country.
Rising out-of-pocket costs are pushing consumers to manage their own care, but direct-to-consumer lab testing for health and wellness is still largely unavailable.
Consumers can collect blood, saliva, or urine at home with kits that measure well-evidenced markers such as food sensitivity, hormones, and fertility.
A virtual physician network authorizes the lab requisition when an order is placed.
The company fulfills the kit and manages logistics across its partner labs.
Unstandardized lab data are translated into a dashboard of results the consumer can understand and act on.
The service complies with direct-to-consumer testing regulations in the states where it operates.
Partner labs are CLIA-certified reference laboratories, and the tests are as accurate as a test a doctor would order.
The company does not share the customer's results data.

Custom currency is hard because payment systems do not track every code and interaction, control who can spend it and when, or tie promotions to gift cards and refunds, so businesses that issue it have to build the system themselves.
A web application and API let a business create, distribute, and manage its own custom currency and redeem it in checkout.
Marketing teams can control, send, and track that custom currency.
The product starts at $90 a month for 1,000 active codes, then $15 a month per additional 1,000, so businesses of any size can use it.
Keeping track of warehouse inventory is manual, slow, and inaccurate, so goods are lost and workers spend hours searching for them.
Flying robots can scan inventory by flying autonomously indoors at centimeter accuracy without GPS, using computer vision and specialized onboard computing.
The current system is built for high-bay selective-rack warehouses with uniform, palletized goods and a label on each pallet.
On-site infrastructure relays what the robots collect to warehouse workers.
Real-time analytics software tells the worker how to correct the count in the warehouse system or on the floor.
Hardware and installation are sold for an upfront setup fee, in the way traditional industrial automation equipment is sold.
The software is sold as a subscription that can add data-driven premiums as the system collects more information.
Medical tourism is dominated by travel agents who lack clinical expertise, which leaves patients with unvetted doctors, poor outcomes, and little trust.
Patients travel to save money against opaque home-country prices, to avoid long waits, or to reach procedures that regulation blocks at home.
Doctors pass a vetting process led by a U.S. physician board that reviews credentials, interviews them, and sometimes watches them operate, and only a small share are accepted.
Patients and doctors communicate in a HIPAA-compliant center with live chat, video, and medical file sharing.
The platform collects documents, records, and payments so the doctors can focus on care.
Outbreak testing is backlogged for months, and current tests are either too insensitive for early detection or too costly and immobile to use near the patient.

A portable chip needs no external pumps, controllers, computers, or valves, costs far less than PCR at manufacturing scale, and uses isothermal nucleic-acid amplification with sensitivity comparable to PCR.
An app tracks GPS, patient information, and test results so health ministries can deploy resources to hotspots.

Use as a human diagnostic depends on integrating sample preparation into the workflow.
Use as a human diagnostic depends on FDA clearance.
Passwords fail because people are forgetful, negligent, or malicious, and replacement tools are not adopted when they require new user behavior or heavy IT integration.
Single sign-on, identity and access management, and enterprise password managers still put sensitive information in the cloud and create a single point of failure.
The user approves a login on the phone with a fingerprint, and the phone pushes the username, password, and SMS two-factor token into the browser.
Administrators have one ecosystem to see logins, revoke access, and grant accounts.
Administrators can limit an account by location, time, and IP address.
Administrators can change a password in the background immediately or on a company-wide schedule.
The product works without integration with the service providers it logs into.
The first five users are free, and each additional user starts at $5.4.99 per month.
Product teams are stuck with delivery tools, scattered feedback, spreadsheets, and disorganized backlogs, so they build features nobody wants.
Integrations bring support tickets, customer conversations, emails, and interview notes into one research place.
Feature ideas are organized by the user needs they serve so teams can see why a feature matters.
A prioritized feature is placed on an auto-generated roadmap that can be shared with the insights behind it.
Chosen features can be pushed to Jira or other engineering systems, and progress is shown back in real time.
The product is a per-user subscription starting at $24 a month, reached through content marketing and inside sales.
Talk media such as podcasts and radio are long and not interactive, so they do not fit mobile-first audiences the way music, photos, and video do.
Users can start bite-sized talk shows on a topic and invite friends or followers into short audio conversations.
After a recording, the app reduces background noise and engineers the voice, and the user can add voice filters and background music.
Users can send private voice messages that disappear after 24 hours.
Creators can share talks on other social platforms and embed them natively on any website.
Brands and top creators can use the platform to create and distribute audio content, not only individual users.
Livestock disease is caught too late, and earlier detection could prevent large losses that the industry now spends heavily to treat.
Historic and real-time data can be put in one standard format and combined with genomics on the animal and the disease to give a comprehensive view of animal health.
Livestock veterinarians can diagnose disease more accurately and efficiently at the point of care and can see potential outbreaks.
Mining the records lets livestock veterinarians find the most efficient and effective treatments.
The platform lets the pharmaceutical industry find new gene targets and pathogens so drug development is faster.
Livestock and pharmaceutical customers are reached through their existing relationships and pay an annual subscription for the tools and data, with extra fees for custom projects.
Getting lawn care typically takes repeated calls, an in-person visit just for a price, a multi-day wait, cash or a check, and a crew that may not show up.
An address alone yields an instant quote, a crew can be scheduled with confidence it will show up, payment is by card, and ratings keep later jobs with the best crews.
Human crews cannot make up rain, breakdowns, or sickness without delays, because a day's capacity is limited and the work cannot be shifted to night.
Consumer robotic mowers cost $1,500 to $5,000, need a buried perimeter wire and a difficult install, and still do not edge, trim, fertilize, or weed.
A technician installs the base and perimeter wire and programs the mower, and the service then monitors it remotely and replaces blades.

The battery mower covers the perimeter and then the center, backs away from obstacles, stops the blades within a second if lifted or tilted, and runs emissions-free on about 11 kilowatt hours a month.
The robotic service costs less than a traditional lawn service, at $99 a month.
Edging, trimming, and fertilizer can be added for an extra fee, using crews already in the field.
People can reach only the contacts they already have, or a bot that cannot yet do more than one automated trick.

A transactional layer lets the user tip the person they chatted with.
Teams create presentations in PowerPoint, discuss them by email and Slack, store them in cloud drives, break the formatting across versions, and need another tool to present or share.

An enterprise version places the product behind the corporate firewall for additional security.
Anyone can sign up for free, and paid plans are offered for individuals and teams.
Audits cannot run on every code change, scanner reports are ignored because they are full of false positives, and firewalls are left too open to avoid blocking legitimate traffic.
Runtime monitoring inside the application watches critical functions and blocks unknown vulnerabilities by logic rather than patterns, which is also how false positives are reduced.
Pricing starts at $99 per month and scales with the number of hosts.
Navigation apps pre-compute routes and assume traffic will not change during the drive, so they price each stretch with the wrong time's traffic and reroute often.
Loop detectors, traffic cameras, and advanced vehicles provide more accurate traffic data than phones, including a real-time feed from road sensors.

A person is not authenticated by an identification number, a photo card, or a password.

Unsupported arches fatigue the feet, pronation or supination misaligns the body, and shoes do not provide enough comfort.

The toy is packed with educational content, including jokes, stories, and scavenger hunts, and is meant to stay engaging over weeks and years rather than one-off answers.

Most commerce is still in physical stores, but brands cannot control in-store execution and still work through calls, email, and costly visits.

Businesses can build, visualize, and analyze their energy data from an energy bill alone.

Showers heat fresh water and throw it away after one use, and using less flow or recovering heat does not stop the waste.

The hardware can be sold for $29.50, or provided free with installation, insurance, and maintenance in exchange for a share of the savings.

Stock music for video is expensive, legally confusing, a poor fit, and already used by many other creators.
An AI system writes original music note by note from music theory and produces it to a professional standard.
Creators get five free tracks a month and then pay about $7 per track at download, about 80% less than elsewhere.

Finding contractors and then running their work across scattered messages and files is informal, slow, and inefficient.
A company's contributor records, past and future, are stored in one place that all of its employees can access.

Invoices are pulled into one place, and a company can approve and distribute payments to as many as 80 countries.

Field professionals have to recreate their site work on a desktop computer, doing the same task two or three times.

ArcSight Pro adds cloud service so professionals can organize field data and collaborate and share it with coworkers.

AI and machine learning help individual contact-center agents and their managers do the job.

Getting safe drinking water has forced a tradeoff between products that do not remove harmful germs and methods that need electricity, pumping, time, or bad-tasting chemicals.
The filter rolls out as a personal bottle, then household and industrial products, and as an inside component for other water products.
Sales start with wellness buyers in the United States and Europe and middle-class buyers in emerging markets, then extend to rural and low-income communities once manufacturing costs fall.

Mobile fragmentation makes developers spend about a third of the development budget on testing, because they must buy many devices and hire people or else risk a bad app-store review.
Existing cloud testing still asks developers to write unit tests and then hands them a long error log, so they spend hours fixing problems without the device in hand.

Inventory and purchases of new devices are driven by demand and by queuing algorithms.
Custom rack shells let devices be added easily inside the data center and keep those devices from overheating.

Even a small web-page change requires a developer or agency, hundreds or thousands of dollars, and days or weeks of waiting, because people who know HTML and CSS are less than 1 percent of the population and everyone else can only fill in a rigid template.

An existing page can be analyzed, broken into its root content, and rebuilt in an editable form that is pixel-for-pixel accurate.
Developers get full access to the source code the product generates and can build custom widgets that extend the platform.

Stores change prices faster and less transparently, sometimes with shoppers' own data, and the guarantees that would return a later drop or a missed coupon are too much hassle to claim, so consumers leave the money uncollected.
The app scans inbox receipts, tracks the prices of what was bought, and automatically files a claim when the price drops.

Receipt and store mail is pulled by subject and sender only, the rest of the inbox stays with the email provider, and the data that is stored is protected with bank-level algorithms, intrusion prevention, and strict access controls.

Video ads that ignore the content are irrelevant, so publishers lose money when viewers skip, brands get a weaker return, and viewers are irritated, because major platforms target from user data and reach.

There has been no easy way to log gym exercises, because a written log does not last and ordinary fitness trackers count only steps.
A smartwatch app automatically identifies exercises, counts repetitions, and tracks calories burned.

Personal trainers can create professional routines, give feedback on workouts, and help users stay motivated toward their goals.

Indoor growers' sensor readings and yield notes stay disconnected, so the records do not explain problems and growers dig through notebooks, pay consultants, or decide by gut.

Companies are still on a legacy desk phone, or on a simple computer softphone that does not add real value.

A cloud service can take the same automation beyond games to other industries and to customers large and small.

Patients have trouble keeping up with manual logging and remembering a twice-daily respiratory medicine, so they miss most doses and can end up in the hospital.

The inhaler sensors and the home spirometer sync wirelessly to a mobile app.
Clinicians can see adherence and spirometry in one snapshot and customize the treatment plan for the time the patient spends outside the clinic.

Home growers face high barriers because quality cannabis requires specialized knowledge of lighting, nutrients, and growing medium, online advice is unreliable, and the alternative is closing off a room or using a large grow tent.
A smartphone-controlled system automatically grows a chosen strain by using a cannabis-specific LED and by dosing nutrients, balancing pH, and controlling temperature, humidity, and odor.

A customized instant manicure is a hassle for girls because salons are inconvenient, expensive, and limited in art, and painting with the non-dominant hand looks poor.
