Students can use files and resources shared by classmates for free, including files from previous semesters.
A campus founder program and a marketing push on the first day of class lead students to invite classmates, friends, and roommates.

Any student can offer on-demand tutoring and earn money, and a stuck student can get a course-matched mentor even late at night for about the price of a beer, because the platform knows when and in which subject help is needed.

Restaurants charge the same price at busy and empty times for perishable tables, about 40 percent of inventory goes unused for lack of yield management, food is wasted because they cannot forecast or price it, and a large share of restaurants fail.
Reservations and food orders from online and offline channels are consolidated in a diary that is integrated with the point-of-sale system.
Analytics show a restaurant's utilization and its revenue per available seat hour.

The restaurant sets a sales or seat-hour goal and rules for overbooking, blackouts, walk-ins, and channel commissions, and the system forecasts demand from many variables and recommends a price for each time slot.

Small businesses need branding such as a logo, cards, a website, and social pages, but crowdsourced professional work costs hundreds or thousands of dollars, so most settle for low-quality do-it-yourself branding they cannot really afford.
A learning system uses thousands of design rules to study the business and generate an original brand without templates, with a very large number of design options from one set of inputs.
The brand package costs fifty dollars, and the customer pays only after approving the design.
The system stays on as a service and keeps designing the offline and online assets the company needs, such as menus, packaging, websites, applications, and social pages.
Brands the system designs are used to derive brand insights and trend insights for the customer.
Technology in the car goes out of date and otherwise requires buying a new car, while systems aimed at new cars leave more than a billion vehicles already on the road uncovered.
A small device plugs in under the dash of a car made after 1996, connects to that car, and lets the driver download an app catalog and use apps immediately.
Beagle alerts a parent when a teen drives recklessly, speeds, or misses school.
eCall detects a crash automatically, in the way an onboard safety service does.
Lock and Key locates the car and alerts the owner if it is stolen.
Auto diagnoses the car and gets bids for the repair.
Insured can lower the driver's insurance premium.
Race logs a video of the trip and hundreds of engine readings in an interface the driver can share.
Drive logs trips, gives the driver feedback, and makes driving social.
An app connects the car to the home.
An app runs with Google Glass.
The basic device and the complete device each cost $149.99, and the complete device adds Bluetooth, LTE, a Wi-Fi hotspot, and advanced crash reporting.
A company can plug devices into its fleet, manage and track that fleet with applications it can customize, and pay $149.99 a year including the device and the data plan.

Developers who previously needed a large investment and were limited to one manufacturer's make and model can build for any car through a simple API, attach their own hardware by a backpack or a wireless link, and use web APIs, mobile and Windows SDKs, a car simulator, forums, granular device and event controls, per-call analytics, and documentation.
Opening the platform to developers is aimed at a connected-car market of more than 400 million vehicles in the US, Europe, and Canada and about $131 billion.
Each use of the bottle records when the cap opens and closes and how much medication is removed, and servers compare that use with the patient's dosage schedule.
The bottle glows during the dosing window and flashes and beeps after that window passes.
Missed-dose reminders can go out by email, text, or automated call, including to a landline and without an app, and can also go to caregivers or family.
The bottle sends its data over the cellular network and works as soon as it comes from the pharmacy, without Wi-Fi or Bluetooth pairing.
A 45-day battery covers a standard 30-day prescription, and a longer prescription needs only an occasional micro-USB charge.
Reminder messages ask why a dose was missed and can alert a clinician in real time, for example so side effects such as nausea can be treated.
An open API lets the bottle integrate with healthcare partners' systems.
Specialty pharmaceutical companies pay for the service and give patients the bottle free with high-cost drugs, because better adherence increases refills and the drug maker's revenue.
Diabetes care is inadequate because manual logging is tedious, available digital tools are incompatible and hard to use, and no platform connects patients to a support network.
A smart cable connects most existing glucometers, including those in emerging markets, to a smart device through the audio jack, so users do not have to replace their meters.
The app flags out-of-range readings, lets the patient tag meals, medication, mood, and food, and turns the log into graphs that can be sent to a doctor.
Readings are stored so a remote partner can view them, encourage the patient, and receive alerts if the patient misses a test or a reading is out of range.
The platform supports third-party interactions such as insurers varying premiums, pharmacies marketing to users, and monetary rewards.
Robots are now limited by expensive, complex hardware, especially actuators, rather than by brains, sensors, or software.
One integrated joint combines the encoder, motor, transmission, and bearings, at about one-tenth the cost of an industrial equivalent and with less bulk and weight.
A servo, a joint, and a link are enough reusable parts to assemble, take apart, and rebuild many kinds of robots.
A phone app programs the hardware on the fly, records keyframes, and repeats sequences wirelessly for rapid prototyping.
A browser-based builder assembles and programs a robot, simulates it in a physics engine, supports sharing, and can place the order.
Sudden infant death syndrome is the leading cause of infant death and a central fear for parents.
Monitors already on the market do not tell parents whether the baby is breathing.
A sock uses pulse oximetry to send heart rate and oxygen to a parent's phone and alert them in an emergency.
The electronics are flexible and sealed in silicone so the sock is waterproof on a baby.
Multiple optical sensors keep a pulse-oximetry reading as an infant's foot grows through the first year.
The sock also reports skin temperature, alerts when the baby rolls onto the stomach, and reports how restless the baby is.
At-home readings can form an infant health dataset used to predict illness, from a cold to life-threatening events.

Seniors fall with traditional walkers when they forget to set the brakes before sitting and when steep ramps make the walker run away, and those injuries are costly and can leave them in worse health.
Pressure sensors brake the walker when the user sits, and accelerometers and encoders apply gradual braking on a descent.
The technology is licensed to walker manufacturers so they can build it into walkers at the factory.
Shoppers cannot reliably find a fashion item by turning a remembered image into a text search.
A photo search returns the same item and similar alternatives, and the results can be narrowed by brand and price.
If automated search misses, a human stylist looks for the item and sends shoppable links.
A social network lets people follow others and shop the searches and results those people share.
Business rules override the image technology when recognition fails.
The company is paid an affiliate commission of 6% on sales.
Most websites have no API, creating one is complex, and web data is therefore available mainly to organizations that can hire developers.
A person can turn a web page into a table and a live cloud API in minutes by showing the tool example rows and columns, without writing code.
APIs created this way can be combined so one call streams data from many sites into an application.
A free version of the product will always remain available.
The Data Factory Chrome extension opens a library of ready-made APIs and extracts a supported page into a table or a live feed.
Bicycle theft is common and costly in Europe and the United States.
Vibration, gyroscope, temperature, and light sensors, plus a wired cable, detect sawing, drilling, impact, heat or cold, and cable cuts, and tampering raises an alarm and a notification.
A GPS tracker locates the lock if the bicycle is stolen.
The lock is opened and closed without a physical key.
Owners can share a bike or rent it out, including across a city, without separate docking infrastructure, and the lock is meant to keep a rented bike safe.
Current voice assistants miss the popular apps people actually use and cover only a few applications.
Voice commands operate popular apps from inside this app, and a request can fall back from one service to another, such as from SoundCloud to Spotify or YouTube.
An API hub works as an IDE so a new service can be connected with a few lines of code.
Voice can reach the data and actions of complex business software such as Salesforce and Google Analytics.
A business with an API can integrate, sell that access in an enterprise store, and this company keeps 20% of the price.
Designers sell professional-level 3D printable files on a marketplace instead of giving the files away.
A buyer who does not see the right product can work directly with designers to have it created.
A network of 3D print shops can make an order for pickup nearby or for shipping, and the system selects the option.
Revenue comes from design sales and from print jobs, and printers compete for the work, which lowers the price.
Ninety-five percent of retail sales still come from brick-and-mortar stores.
Shoppers get rich personalization online, but in a store brands see only anonymous transactions with no personality.
Brands find it difficult to tell how the business is doing from their retail data.
The point-of-sale system can identify the kind of purchaser a shopper is and send a receipt that includes recommended products.
A visual dashboard lets brands see how sales are doing and what they can do about it.
The company goes after standalone fashion brands, rather than mass merchandisers, because those brands care about giving customers the best experience.
Building a mobile app is hard and expensive because it requires specialized technical skills, and even a simple app costs thousands of dollars and months of waiting.
The apps produced are native, which gives users the best look, feel, and performance.
A preview app lets the builder test and interact with the app live on their own mobile device while building it.

People in traditional enterprises cannot get work done on personal devices because the apps they need sit behind the corporate firewall, and mobile device management locks the whole device and forces IT to add data-center boxes.
The product connects through the enterprise's existing SSL VPNs, including Cisco, Juniper, Dell, and F5, so IT installs no new data-center boxes and can be running in minutes.
The product collects work-context activity on the device and turns it into Insights for user experience and problems and Events for audit and compliance.
Access and control are given away free, and the company charges for end-user activity data.
Insurance brokers earn generous commissions and are legally barred from rebating them, so the company provides services and software for free instead of giving money back.
Payroll can be set up online without faxing, or an existing payroll system can be connected in both directions so employee and deduction data move both ways.

A client can name a carrier and policy number and sign to make the company broker of record, which lets it manage the health plan and collect the commission while the plan, price, and cards stay the same.

Hiring takes only a few inputs, after which the company generates the offer and IP documents from the client's templates, collects payroll and work-eligibility information, enrolls benefits, and writes the employee into the payroll system.
Only about 20 percent of HR is strategic, and about 80 percent is administrative paperwork such as payroll and benefits enrollment.
It is inefficient to call many local merchants to find one who will take an appointment, even though qualified small businesses have idle time and will work hard to win a new customer.
A customer can place a request for a personal service and set the price, travel distance, time, and a minimum merchant rating.
A submitted bid offers the customer to nearby businesses, flipping the usual process of filtering through business listings.
When a merchant accepts a bid, the customer's card is charged immediately and the service is scheduled on both calendars.
Merchants pay nothing upfront, receive customers who have already put a card behind the offer, know when the service will happen, and accept only when they have excess capacity.
Customers are connected only to verified, rated local businesses, not to other consumers.
Finding ideas is a huge problem because people and companies lose good ideas.
Files are discovered across any repository, including email, desktop, and third parties.
Each file is stripped of its container and formatting so that only individual components remain, such as pages, charts, text, and images.
Each component is indexed and normalized so one search returns the best page, not the whole file, ranked by the relevance of its content and context.
Natural language processing tells the user what the content is about, so nothing has to be tagged.
Components are shown as a visual collage that can be mashed up across file formats, exported to PowerPoint or PDF, shared as a visual email, or saved and opened from anywhere.
The product belongs to everyone, not only large enterprises, and a Dropbox account is enough to use it.
Open or free software has bugs and missing features, and support is hard to get.
A user can pay, or a developer can get paid, by placing an incentive directly from an issue page.
The company takes a 6 percent fee on each successful incentive.
Sharing food with others is a basic human need that already exists and will continue.
Most tourists want to meet locals and have an authentic dining experience.
A guest can find a hosted event, see the place, the other attendees, and the reviews, and pay securely online, with the commission included in the payment.
Verified hosts have their events protected by a one-million-dollar guarantee.

Public data is technically public but not accessible, because it lives in incompatible portals, files, and old databases, cannot be searched across, and is siloed so the connections between sources stay invisible.
A browser plugin highlights companies, people, and locations on a webpage and routes a click into that same public-data detail.
Geometric and photorealistic data are captured with a camera the company has modified, including a digital SLR whose texture and lighting it controls.
The capture is turned into a photorealistic 3D model that a user can walk through with full control over navigation, including views that flat images cannot provide.
Every space they construct is streamed both on the web and on the iPad.
An end user can edit the 3D model directly, changing the time of day and lighting, placing and recoloring furniture, and swapping entire layouts.
A contract runs through drafts, approvals, negotiations, revisions, and signatures, and that process becomes unmanageable when each rep juggles many contracts across a large organization.
Managers can see in one dashboard how many deals are in legal, stuck in negotiation, or out for customer signature.
Students can upload pictures, videos, audio, embedded content, and documents into a project portfolio.
An algorithm pairs a student with colleges that match the subjects they work on.
Badges in subjects such as chemistry, molecular engineering, aeronautics, and robotics keep students excited about uploading projects.
Email clients and task managers have each failed to solve the problem on their own.
Priorities have to be captured from the inbox, from your mind, and from meetings into one place.
Triage means deciding what to do with everything in the inbox, using the Handlebar so those decisions can be made quickly.
Doing the work shows the instructions, comments, links, and communication thread for the task so it can be finished without context switching.
People are pushed to eat more than they need, most are overweight or obese, and today's diet solutions show a lack of imagination.
Meals are planned from high-quality restaurant food delivered to home and office, with the convenience of a personal assistant and the personalization of a nutritionist, done through technology.
Local restaurant kitchens supply healthy food custom-made to health and taste preferences and hand-delivered within the hour.
The service attracts people who would never have joined a commercial weight-loss plan or eaten diet food from a box.
Consumers pay $28 a month as a subscription fee.
Restaurants pay about $16 per user per month in commissions for the additional traffic.
People outside New York City can use a free iPhone or Android app so they can still eat healthy.
Households spend half their energy bill heating and cooling, several rooms are overheated or overcooled, and thermostats are only part of the solution.
A wirelessly networked vent automatically redirects air from the home's central heating or cooling system.
A short questionnaire about the home and habits programs each vent's open and close schedule so the system is running in minutes.
The vent is sold on the web through e-commerce partnerships and then through retail outlets such as Lowe's and Home Depot.
A four-vent system is sold either for $25 plus $4 a month for smart-cycle programming, management, and push notifications, or for $150 with no monthly fee.
Home builders, HVAC suppliers, and utility companies will sell the vent to their customers with a subsidy.
Non-networked matching vents are sold so a customer can keep a uniform look across the vents in the home.
People hand out keys to friends and often do not get them back.
A chip in the apartment intercom opens the front door downstairs, with no changes to that front door.
An internet-connected lock opens the apartment door, and partners such as Kwikset supply the security and reliability.
Keys can be shared with friends and guests, set to be temporary, and removed at any time.
The owner can monitor who accessed each door and when.
Regular keys or a PIN code still open the apartment if the phone battery runs low or the phone is lost.
Large amounts of data sit in email attachments, which wastes that data and slows work down.
Files in email can be moved directly into other cloud services and kept associated with the original email.
A file attached from the cloud can be limited to the designated recipients so it is shared securely.
An admin can set policies across the cloud applications a team uses so data is handled consistently.
Individual users pay nothing, and a customer pays only when claiming a group and governing the data workflow across that group.
College recruiting is increasingly competitive, good candidates have many options, and a startup or mid-sized company has to compete with big employers on campus.
A platform lets college recruiting teams build and manage relationships with students over multiple years.
Companies can create programming, design, or business challenges that students solve while interacting with people at the company.
Students can showcase in-class or outside projects and get feedback from professionals at the company.
Students always use it free, and companies pay a monthly subscription.
Developers who want cross-platform apps need a backend to sync data across devices, and the current options are limited to Apple, take months to build, or become expensive at scale.
The mobile and web backend stores app data in the user's personal cloud, such as Dropbox or Google Drive.
The developer pays for a license and the app user does not.
Meeting details and content are scattered across the calendar, photos, a notebook, and email, so finding what happened takes forever if it was recorded at all.
Once enough people on a team use it, a premium service integrates meeting and contact data with cloud storage, CRMs, and task-management systems.
Good doctors make bad decisions because they have no way to share their experience and have to rely on reference tools that do not match what actually works.
SharePractice structures and shares verified doctors' experience as a curated list of treatments ranked by upvotes and downvotes, with comments from other doctors on why a choice is best.
Sharing a case with doctor contacts sends a structured question, stores the structured answer in the reference, and brings the responding doctor in as a user.
A proprietary medical ontology combines treatment and diagnosis databases so that variants in medical terminology are recognized as the same condition.
SharePractice captures why a physician chose one treatment over another, information that ordinary prescription records do not contain.

Retail shippers of diverse, non-standard goods cannot readily price packing and shipping, because carrier markets are fragmented and will not quote an item unless it is in a box, a crate, or on a pallet.
A real item is converted into packed weights and dimensions, which produces instant packing quotes and instant shipping quotes.
The shipper can schedule a pickup at home or the office or drop the item at a ShipHawk network location, including local delivery by the same agent, then pay and print the receipt and label.
ShipHawk is paid a commission by the shipping, packing, and insurance providers it sends business to.
Spacebar streams live audio performances to mobile phones, and a listener anywhere can hear a five-minute free preview and then join the show for 99 cents.
Bands receive data they have not had before, which helps them plan tours, and venues receive business intelligence for booking acts.

A buyer enrolls suppliers, collects scorecards, and drills into which suppliers in a region drive a problem such as water pollution, raising or lowering how much that issue counts, as supply-chain risk analysis on the fly.
Suppliers see where they stand relative to industry peers and are incentivized to improve because keeping their relationships with buyers depends on it.
A buyer can see anonymous scores of suppliers outside its own supply chain, so more sustainable suppliers get more business.
A unified scorecard library ranks questionnaires by popularity of use so companies send the same questionnaires and a supplier enters answers once, which reduces RFP fatigue.
Text and voice messaging each fail in ordinary situations, because voice added to text has to be corrected and voice cannot be used in a meeting or in class.
Talks puts text and voice in every message, and the original audio remains when the transcription is imperfect.
People can post to social networks such as Twitter and Facebook as easily as sending a message to a friend.
The messaging app supports pictures, video, doodles, music, and location as well as voice.
Talks is coming out on four platforms, iOS now and Android, Windows Phone, and BlackBerry in the coming weeks.
The receiver does not need the Talks app, so a message can be sent to anyone regardless of their device or which apps they have.
Voice cloning learns the user's voice from speech to the app and keeps a cloud clone so a message or social post is read aloud in that voice or in a celebrity's voice.
Online fraud is an enormous cost to e-commerce merchants and is growing faster than commerce, while human review cannot keep scaling and existing identity questions destroy conversion.

Trustive is a real-time identity platform that uses social data as the primary signal, adds behavioral and transactional data, and returns the merchant a score of whether the buyer is who they say they are.
Trustive pre-populates the checkout form with the customer's name, address, and email so the purchase is smoother, easier, and more secure.
Developers connect the platform with a JavaScript module, a Magento plug-in, and a REST API, and merchants pay only per transaction, with no annual contract and no monthly minimum.
As children play, skills are tracked and turned into personalized learning profiles that recommend games and offline activities for lagging skills and that encourage healthy habits.
A patented cloning and remote coaching system lets parents, educators, and extended family enter the game, collaborate, and give progressive hints inside a closed social network.
Parents can invite an experts and mentors network into the game to coach the child and to share data for targeted skill development.
The platform is open to developers who use the neural algorithmic learning model to make games that develop children's skills with scientific credibility.
One system supplies the telecommunications APIs and functions that had been split across telco, business-phone, and developer products.
A cell phone used as a business phone does not provide extension dialing, call recording, or time-of-day routing.

Tying the handset into the switch puts each cell call onto a carrier voice channel and through the switch's business logic as the call is placed, which is what provides bring-your-own-device activation, seamless transfer, presence, location without GPS, extension dialing, recording, and live transcription.
Because the network does not need internet access, a customer such as a government, a military user, a hospital, or a bank can run a private telecom network.
International calls routed through the switch over IP are far cheaper than traditional carrier international rates.
Email does not let a mobile team share files, talk, and calendar together, so people cannot work with a group from the phone.
The team works in a structured messaging stream and can search that stream even when the conversation has gone on for years.
Files shared in the conversation can be reviewed in one place, including files integrated from Dropbox and Google Drive.
A dynamic poll can sit inside a post, and the author can see how the team voted.
A person can create a calendar event in the stream and the whole team receives it without anyone else having to do anything.
People are invited from Zula, phone contacts, Facebook, LinkedIn, and Google+, and a deep link opens that conversation directly.
One tap starts a conference call with the people in the stream; they join without phone numbers, and the call can be kept and recorded.
Consumer wearables and GPS watches are motivators rather than professional tools, because GPS can be off by about 15 feet.
Real-time motion tracking needs multiple observation points at once, so a swing's angle and strength can be read together with acceleration and position.

Inch-accurate position, which is patented, comes from analyzing satellite signals instead of trusting GPS, fusing motion readings from the devices and an access point, and correcting the signal with differential GNSS.
The tracker is a platform whose APIs expose acceleration, position, and speed for other software to use.
Team sports have no technology for a real-time tactical analyzer, for injury prevention, or for talent scouting.
Most men still shop for clothes offline because they do not know where to start online and do not trust that an item will fit unless they try it on.
A marketplace can connect men who hate shopping with people who love to shop, because choosing clothes is personal and takes a human who can find items the man would not find himself.
A learning engine records what a man likes and does not like, his sizes, and his style, so shoppers can be matched to him and later shoppers can reuse that profile.

Men can try a couple of sizes and return what they do not want by choosing a pickup time and place, without repackaging or a post office trip, and they are charged only for what they keep plus a tip for the shopper.
People with a sense of style and time available, who do not have to be fashion experts, will make money by shopping for these men.
Text input efficiency has fallen because people now type on tablets rather than on keyboards they can feel.
Because glass has no tactile keys, the on-screen keyboard moves to the fingers so the home row forms underneath them.
Taps are distinguished from resting fingers by sensing the vibration of a thump with the accelerometer together with the touch sensor.
The keyboard is for people who can type without looking, including two-finger and four-finger typists, not only ten-finger typists.
The keyboard will be licensed directly to device makers so they can embed it.
The keyboard will also be offered to application developers so they can embed it in an app.
Typing with this keyboard is about twice as fast as current tablet solutions, and the algorithm keeps improving.
Using music online increases spending, time in the venue, and perception of the brand.
Putting music online is a large legal undertaking covering lawyers, copyright payments, and internet-radio rules.
A legal turnkey service adds popular music to a website, app, or game and takes care of the licensing.
A customer can play their own music from a digital workspace instead of a curated station.
Analytics and A/B testing let a customer check whether music lifts engagement, retention, and revenue.
Popular music streaming is offered self-serve at $25 per month for a website, app, or game.
A minute of finished video can take many hours of post-production because teams coordinate through email threads, meetings, calls across time zones, and spreadsheets.
A viewing room keeps the cut and the feedback together, pausing the video for a timestamped comment and resuming when the comment is sent.
A timestamped comment can be turned into an edit, assigned to an editor, and delivered as a notification.
Feedback can be exported directly into the editor's video software, and the markers show up in that timeline.
The tool is browser-based and uses the team's existing video hosting, so IT does not have to set up new infrastructure.
Pricing is project-based and friendly to teams of all sizes, affordable for small teams while producing more revenue from larger clients.
The product is being brought into line with Motion Picture Association of America standards used for studio work.
Shoppers cannot easily tell how furniture chosen online or in a store will look in their own home.
Current 3D model tools are too difficult, too expensive, or too slow for homeowners, so almost no homeowners use them.
A homeowner can create a 3D model of a room in a few minutes by photographing each wall with a smartphone app that also uses the gyro, accelerometer, and magnetometer.
A shopper can place furniture from a retailer catalog into the model of their own room.
The model can be shared so a homeowner can collaborate with an interior designer.
The business connects furniture retailers with homeowners.
Software teams lose time because development environments do not match production, tests take too long, and a broken build blocks the whole team.
Each code change is held aside so a breaking change is isolated from the other engineers and does not break the shared build.
Each change is tested in replicas of the production environment, including on a cloud system behind the company's firewall, so the test environment matches production.
The automated test suite is split and run in parallel across those replicas, so engineers are not waiting on one long test run.
Customer-service callers lose time waiting on hold, spelling out their details, and starting over when the call drops.
The caller's profile is sent to the answering agent through an API when the call is placed, so the caller never has to spell a name, email, or address.
Businesses skip the hold line for callers who have already provided their information and route that person as the next caller.
A caller can store billing details and release them from a secure server to the merchant's payment gateway with a four-digit PIN instead of reading a card aloud.
Caller profiles are sold to businesses for 10 cents, which is a saving of over 90 percent versus manual identification.
Major telephone companies supply caller information, so a person can be identified without signing up.
Play has become digital and isolating, with interaction happening through devices rather than face to face with physical objects.
Software running on the iPad recognizes ordinary unmarked pieces in real time, locally, with no network, no calibration, and on any background or lighting.
The current business is selling physical games that come with an iPad app, with the base priced under $30 and the games priced from $15 to $30.
Phones need to charge wirelessly without being taken out of a pocket or a bag.
The charger can safely deliver one watt at 30 feet to multiple devices across a home, returning power only along open paths to each receiver, including behind walls and around corners.
Four core patents have been issued in the United States, and further patents have been issued internationally.
The technology is in the final stages of FCC certification.
Oil and gas operations can use wireless power for sensors and avoid the spark risk of wired power.
Government policy is still communicated as unstructured text, so the public does not engage with changes that affect income and that it barely influences or understands.
Tax returns and census records can be merged into a model of the U.S. economy that lets people configure policies and see projected impacts on real people.
A citizen endorsement is recorded in government analytics and helps shape policy around what people want.
Government tools can already project this information, but they are inaccessible to the public.
A turnkey simulator can replace the enormous sums governments spend on consulting systems, saving money and producing better governing.
Recipients must ride to an agency, wait in line for hours, visit another agency to pay bills, and lose as much as 10 percent to Western Union.
Immigrants can send a credit by SMS to a family's cell phone in Latin America and use it for food, medicine, utility bills, and tuition.
Customers can start a transfer online or at partner mom-and-pop stores.
A recipient can transfer part of the credit to another person, which makes the service viral and builds a social network on top of remittances.
Contracts for 7,200 retail locations in eight countries are what let the service scale.
Retailers pay a fee that subsidizes a flat customer fee of three dollars, up to 70 percent cheaper than alternatives.
Logging in means hunting for the right token or phone app, and the one-time code often changes before it can be typed.
Login is confirmed by holding the phone close to the computer, without unlocking the phone or tapping anything on it.
Patent-pending ultrasonic audio, inaudible to people and detectable by microphones, connects the phone and the computer.
Each session uses a unique key that is encoded into the audio signal, encrypted for the phone, and delivered only when the phone is close, so only that user can confirm the session.
The same proximity method can replace the entire login, with no username, password, or typing.
Because it runs in the browser, it is platform-agnostic, needs no new hardware for users or the data center, and is as simple to set up as it is to use.
An institution can mark where customers may or may not log in, so large transactions can be limited to places such as home or the office.
People already measure steps and sleep, but understanding brain health and emotional wellbeing matters more.
Scientific, patented games show how personality, states of cognition, and emotions drive daily performance.
The app gives personalized recommendations the user can apply immediately.
Connecting biometric devices such as Fitbit adds a holistic view of the other factors in the user's health.
A premium tier adds games and reports that can be shared with family, doctors, or coaches.
Everyday language barriers, including work and medical visits, are not solved by machine translation or algorithms.
A remote human interpreter can translate a speaker into another language in real time.
A hybrid of professional interpreters and crowdsourced bilinguals, who train on video and are rated up by professionals, is how the service covers many languages.
Matching uses the interpreter's languages, proficiency, dialect, and accent.
Interpreters set weekly availability and accept or decline requests pushed to their phone.
A small share of customers drives about half of a local business's revenue, while punch cards and check-in apps take too much work and are not personalized to spending, interests, or identity.
Customers add their credit cards and earn points by paying as they usually do, with no punch card, phone, or NFC at the register.
Rewards and perks are custom-tailored to how much the customer spends, what they are interested in, and who they are.
The business needs no software or hardware integration because redemption works with the equipment it already has.
The business can see who is in the store in real time, including a photo, social-media presence, and how much that person has spent.

The app also shows leasing options for cars, in a region where about 1% of cars on the road are leased versus about 60% in the US and EU.
The online tutoring system, built from scratch, provides note-sharing, whiteboarding, and video.
Once a session is done, the student rates the tutor and receives a progress report.
Tutor hiring is automated: applicants submit documents and interviews, and a machine-learning algorithm helps pre-select candidates.
Tutors are charged a 20% commission per transaction.
Institutions, universities, and schools will be charged $1,000 per month for analytics about their students' tutoring activities.
Hackers can take steering, braking, and acceleration out of the driver's hands, and that threat is real today.
Patents are registered for this vehicle-protection technology.
Fleet owners are offered cybersecurity as a service at $10 per vehicle per month, including continuous updates to the fleet.

Under a revenue-sharing model, an automotive OEM deploys the security in its vehicles, and an insurance company, wireless carrier, or traditional security company provides the subscription to the fleet owner.
Scaling to a vehicle deployment depends on integrating the software with automotive hardware.
A person can have a concussion with no signs or symptoms, and athletes in that situation are often returned to play.
A statistical computer-vision algorithm reads the iris response to a light stimulus, and a neural network classifies whether the person has head trauma.
The diagnostic system is HIPAA compliant.
A test costs 99 cents, and institutions can pay $99 per month for unlimited testing, an unlimited number of profiles, and a dashboard that tracks player health.
Injection molding and CNC machining are slow and expensive ways to make production-quality parts, and 3D printing is faster but makes weaker parts.
The machine makes parts in off-the-shelf manufacturing materials, including plastic, silicone, rubber, copper, and stainless steel.
The process 3D-prints a mold, injects it with off-the-shelf manufacturing material, dissolves the mold, and, for metal, puts the part in a furnace.
A patented shell material that is washed away is critical to the process.
The machine is 5 to 60 times faster and 3 to 125 times less expensive, and it starts from a wall plug with no skilled labor or special ventilation required.
The first customers are service bureaus and rapid prototyping shops, followed by medical and automotive manufacturers that benefit from rapid iteration.
High-definition cameras are passive and do not help in the moment, and human remote monitoring is too expensive for most businesses, so calls for help usually come after the robber is gone.

A human-in-the-loop AI platform detects weapons, masks, and after-hours intruders, lets analysts monitor 500 or more feeds instead of 15 to 20, alerts an analyst within fractions of a second so police can be contacted during the crime, and keeps false positives for retraining.
The workflow combines the quality and reach of professional services with the scale and process control of SaaS tools.
The AI localizes a fetal malformation and gives the obstetrician feedback so the abnormality does not go unnoticed and appropriate intervention can be taken.
Information extracted from the exam automates reporting and documentation and can save up to eight minutes per patient.
The solution is sold to hospitals on a subscription for baseline costs plus volume-based pricing for API calls to the algorithms.

Property managers lack the tools to judge whether rent will be paid, so they require payment on the 1st, late fees by the 3rd, eviction notices by the 5th, certified checks, and first month, last month, and deposit up front.
Owner-operators need a fully online payment system integrated into their accounting software to reduce resident payment risk.
Residents can schedule an online certified payment that the owner can treat as certain when it reaches the bank.

Installment loans at checkout let residents spread move-in costs or a tight month over time, decided in seconds from rent and bank data, while the owner is paid up front and only one loan is open at a time.
The service is free to property owners, is sold through management groups with many properties, and earns revenue from loan origination and payment-processing fees.
Credit is broken for most Americans: many scores are subprime, people are afraid to check them, most reports contain an error, and bad credit costs thousands of dollars a year.
A decision-tree conversation captures feelings and goals, then a credit checkup links the report and prescribes how to resolve questionable items.
Behavioral economics then sets a concrete list of actions that continue to improve the score.
The process yields psychographic, behavioral, and historical credit data that can be turned into user segments and personas.
The company makes money by referring improved users to matching financial products.
It will also build its own flexible financial products for those users.

A data fabric connects important data across silos, stores business logic, adapts in real time when the data or model changes, leaves existing applications in place, and lets users build applications on the linked data.
Most shoppers do not know what they are buying or putting on their faces, and many cosmetic ingredients are harsh chemicals that can make skin worse.
The system classifies people into more than 30 skin types on five dimensions and recommends products from the person's skin profile, similar people's preferences, and age.
A human advisor cross-checks the system and narrows the result to one product.
The user can buy that product through a checkout link using Apple Pay, PayPal, or a credit card.
Current protocols have limited range and connectivity and are often hardware-restricted, so people still use key fobs, phone pairing, and paper tickets to connect or get in.
Data can be sent over silent audio just above human hearing to supplement those connections.
Data over audio is sold as a service per device per year.
Logos in messaging do little, and finding or sharing information while texting means leaving the conversation to search other apps.
Deep linking aggregates data across a suite of services and packages it inside familiar logos in the messaging thread.
Anyone can add a logo profile, the brand can later edit it, and a missing logo can be created instantly from Google.
A brand can sponsor its logo for premium placement, branded content, customizations, app-to-app integrations, and logo analytics.
More data sources, formats, and access frequency make inter-company data hard to manage both technically and operationally.
An operations team can give and get data through an intuitive workflow that turns an ad hoc engineering task into a scalable process.
The platform handles end-to-end encryption, access control, and anonymization.
The platform learns the data and alerts users when schema, quality, or volume changes.
Infrastructure is moving to the public cloud, where attackers can get past perimeter defenses and a breach will happen.
Traditional encryption has significant performance and functionality drawbacks.
Proxy re-encryption protects data on-prem and in the cloud by embedding access controls in the encryption, so only valid users can read it and an intruder sees ciphertext.
The technology complies with NIST and FIPS.
Open-source Hadoop and Kafka offerings make the encryption available for those systems.
People who want to be music artists either lack access to quality producers or cannot afford to pursue music.
Producers lack relationships with artists to whom they can sell their production.
A mobile marketplace lets users discover beats and create original songs with producers for under $5.
Users can write and record songs onto those beats.
Users can also shoot a video for the song they just created.
Users can share that song across social networks, including the product's own network, and turn friends into fans.
Because the songs are original content, the platform does not rely on major-label licensing.
Service professionals cannot reliably find vetted sub-renters, so turnover creates operational and financial strain, and a lease's geography limits where they can work.
A space owner only has to create a listing for vetted renters to find them.
Focusing first on the supply of bookable space is what generates network effects and high retention.
One platform lets a consumer discover, book, manage, pay for, or provide any service, and lets a professional find customers, manage a schedule, and book space.
No one product addresses the whole service industry, and an industry-agnostic platform is necessary for long-term success.
Resume screening that rewards well-known schools and employers, and keyword search, misses most high-potential candidates and surfaces false positives.
Deep computer vision and natural language processing turn each resume, including PDFs and images, into a structured profile.
A general layer trained on millions of career paths qualifies experience and hidden relationships, including across technical and non-technical jobs and languages, rather than keyword skills alone.
A second layer fits assessment to a company's own data and keeps learning from recruiters' decisions.
A one-line widget on a company's site captures more applicants by reducing an application to a simple drop.
Pricing starts at $99 and scales as the recruiter grows.
Clothing returns are a shape problem, not only a size problem, because design is taught on two of nine body shapes and that choice leaves out half of women.
A shape filter captures a shopper's shape and proportion, classifies the assortment, and recommends garments using each garment's design details.
Mental health conditions are common, most people who are diagnosed get no care, and spending on therapists still misses many of those at highest risk.
Anonymous, therapist-moderated groups of five to seven people combine always-available peer text support with scheduled voice therapy.
Natural language processing flags messages with suicidality or maliciousness, including latent wording and conversational context, so providers intervene immediately.
Organizations that already have providers license the technology, pay the company, and patients are not charged.
Spinal screws are often misplaced because surgeons cannot see inside the vertebra, and current navigation goes unused because the view is on a distant screen and is uncomfortable to use.
A see-through visor projects the patient's anatomy onto the surgeon's retina in real time with surgical precision and depth perception, including where a tracked tool is aiming.
The visor is integrated into existing surgical navigation and medical imaging systems and sold together with those systems.
Most people still lack internet access, and neither large connectivity projects nor standalone offline apps will reach them at scale soon.

An SDK meshes phones over Bluetooth so apps work offline, hopping messages past one device's range without flooding the network or draining the battery, including between Android and iOS and with encryption.
The SDK is sold to developers who already have users, and they pay only for monthly active users who use the technology.
Layer hatcheries cannot tell an egg's sex, so billions of male chicks are hatched and killed because they do not lay eggs and are too skinny to sell as meat.
A non-invasive scan through the shell before incubation identifies male eggs so they can be sold as eggs instead of being hatched.
A commercial layer breed that lays sex-detectable eggs is being developed.
Cable charging fails when cords break, disappear, or are forgotten, and charging pads still prevent use of the phone, look poor, and charge only one device per section.
A safe magnetic platform that is FCC compliant can power multiple devices at any angle, without requiring the device to lie perfectly parallel to a receiver.
Cases are needed for popular older phones and for tablets that lack magnetic receivers, while upcoming phones that support the magnetic standard do not need a case.
Direct sales to consumers can sustain gross margins above 50 percent and a high lifetime value because a buyer will want units in several rooms and the office.
The platform is opened for use by existing consumer-electronics manufacturers.
Braille interfaces to computers cost several thousand dollars and show only a few words because they use bulky piezoelectric technology, and that keeps literacy among children low.
A membrane bonded to an electrical actuator deforms each braille dot through an airflow channel, so a tablet can raise a full page of dots without mechanical elements.
Cloud software converts text files, documents, and whole web pages into braille and sends them to the tablet.
The tablet is priced at an affordable 500 dollars and is sold first on the website.
Distribution then scales through global distributors and into developing countries.
Pregnancy complications are rising, and prenatal visits are inconvenient, expensive, and limited by decades-old technology.

A wearable sensor on a disposable patch measures electrical signals from the mother's heart, the uterus, and the baby's heart, and the app uses that to show contraction timing, with further maternal and fetal measures added by software.
Mothers first get a reusable sensor and disposable patches on a monthly subscription they can return after birth, with later sales through referrals and channel partners.
After FDA clearance, reimbursement is meant to make the product standard of care that doctors use.
Crowdsourced maternal and fetal data powers cloud machine learning so doctors can predict and manage complications earlier.
The venture addresses traffic problems, air pollution, and Asian scooters that are low quality, out of fashion, and short of take.
Monroe 2.0 is a fully electric clean-energy e-bike.
A removable aluminum-ion battery is more environmentally friendly than a lithium-ion battery, and four battery packs can go up to about 200 km.
High-power Philips LED lights give the rider extended visibility at night.
Tail lights are embedded in the side of the bike for a sleeker, more modern look.
The motor they designed starts more smoothly and runs more efficiently.
A customization system, made possible with additive manufacturing, lets buyers choose the steering wheel, color, and components, which has traditionally been costly.
The bike is targeted at people who use it for daily community travel, who want to replace old-fashioned scooters, and who want to carry it for trips.
The retail price starts at $1,700, and orders can be placed through the site and by email.
Commercial job sites face water leaks, mold that can grow within 48 hours, and fire damage, and most have no active fire monitoring.

A real-time, end-to-end job-site monitoring network provides active warning and damage mitigation, logistics data for equipment placement and personnel exposure, and a stored history of how the building was built.
Magnets, a hanging strap, and a wrap let sensors stick to metal, hang on a finished wall, or attach to a pipe or 2x4 so they can be moved around a dynamic job site.
A deployment workflow digests the floor plan, places sensors at token locations, and produces a risk audit before the system goes live.
More than 155 mobile-money wallets run isolated from one another, which makes cross-network, cross-border, and online payments difficult.
A single API lets online merchants accept cash and mobile-money wallets, with a high conversion rate, blockchain-ledger security, and easier processing for the unbanked across currencies.
A patented blockchain tunneling network secures and interconnects payment channels so they can be used for cross-network, cross-border, and online payments globally.
A split-payment feature lets a payer pay the part they have and invite other people to pay the rest.
Merchants can disperse and dispatch payments to sellers.
The platform can hold money for marketplaces.
The platform can top up airtime to any prepaid mobile phone in Africa across 42 countries.
The platform charges a monthly fee and a transaction fee.

Multi-channel selling is tedious, time-consuming, and hard to manage in real time because merchants must switch platforms and repeat listing, order, sales-tracking, and inventory work on every channel.
Merchants can connect stores, automatically import products, add the information a new channel requires, and publish those listings from one dashboard.
Automated real-time inventory synchronization imports orders and updates stock on other channels so merchants do not have to make manual changes, go out of stock, or oversell.
The product is an affordable solution optimized for small businesses.
Viewers can stream the service on a mobile app and on TV.
Cloud data is processed in massive energy-guzzling data centers that face growing pressure from media and AI demand and from rising microchip costs.
Twelve billion devices sit idle in pockets and on desks.
The software harnesses everyday devices for intensive tasks such as video encoding, generative AI, and 3D rendering.
Millions of remote sports fans are disconnected from the stadium.
Fans using connected devices can transmit their energy straight into the stadium.
A vibe board graphically represents fan energy, and fans can contribute to it from a smartphone app.
Sound capture shows average decibel volume by country and compares it with decibel meters in the stadium so teams can see which fans are loudest.
The system captures a unique set of fan data that can feed CRM activities.
A fan chip priced at $4 plugs into any merchandise to make it connected, and smartware apps for iOS and Android can be downloaded onto an existing device.
Fans at games waste time finding food, drinks, restrooms, and each other, and ordinary mobile apps do not address those fan problems.
A crowd-sourced social map helps fans find tailgates, parking, food, and beer.
The Meet Me feature lets a fan see exactly where friends are in the crowd.
An official Ticketmaster integration lets fans purchase tickets to sporting events.

Choosing drug targets and compounds is the critical first stage of drug discovery, and it is slow, expensive, and often subjective because teams must manually assess scattered data on thousands of proteins and can filter out the best targets.
Pricing depends on the number of compounds or targets to be analyzed.

Most of the money spent putting the right information in front of people is wasted because marketers and product managers are overwhelmed by data, people are highly diverse and change over time, and historical likes, cohorts, segments, and A/B tests do not target a person at the current moment.
Machine learning married to fast infrastructure processes each user action and returns it to the site in a 125-millisecond round trip, treating every impression as a cohort of one in real time.

Patients behind closed doors may be resting, deteriorating in bed, out of bed and in trouble, or already dead, but four-hour wired rounds wake every patient and can miss events, and cameras alone do not proactively alert staff to deterioration.
Video analytics, the first go-to-market phase, detect whether a person in a room is in bed or out of bed.
Scarce clinician time has to go to the most urgent situations, and patients need to be stepped down from hospitals to cheaper places such as nursing settings, care homes, and their own homes.
Large-audience streaming through a content delivery network introduces about one to two minutes of latency.
Real-time streaming, defined as under half a second, does not scale to enough concurrent viewers.
Customers can optionally add Proximity Multicast, peer-to-peer algorithms that further reduce cost, extend scale, and ease bandwidth constraints.
People are getting better at creating their own video.
Video is split between a tightly controlled studio and agency industry and uncurated user-generated content.
The company gives clients tools to produce high-impact video at scale by having their own fans, customers, and employees film, rather than building a separate creator community.
Clients can search content by sentiment, object recognition, and transcription.
Clients can edit by dragging videos in the online tools or by moving selected videos into their own editing programs.
Freelance editors can log into a client's studio remotely and create the needed video within a few days.
The platform is sold as a subscription rather than pay-as-you-go.

Parents of school-going children face five pain points: a communication gap with the school, the child's safety and health, instant progress and behaviour reports, having to be present to pay fees, and daily needs such as uniforms and stationery.
The app provides two-way communication between parents and teachers.
Parents receive the report card instantly.
GPS tracking shows where the child is, for the child's security.
Parents can pay school fees online in the app instead of going to the school.
Uniforms and stationery can be bought in the app and delivered home.
The company targets private mid-high and upper high-end schools in India, a segment of about 30,000 schools.
People spend most of their time indoors, where unseen carbon dioxide rises to about three times outdoor levels and, at those levels, cognitive performance falls sharply.
Most ventilation systems recirculate the same air and take little from outside, because conditioning outside air uses a lot of energy, so fresh air still has to come from outside.
Biochips of photosynthetic chlorella, inoculated into a chip and powered by LEDs, absorb carbon dioxide and produce oxygen more efficiently than trees.
The closed system uses replaceable cartridges, like air filters, three or four times a year to replenish nutrients and remove waste.
The company first sells custom systems and standard units to businesses.
Distributors, including HVAC partners, sell the systems in addition to direct sales.
Drinking water in many cities contains lead, arsenic, mercury, and other heavy metals.
Ordinary filters do not remove smaller particles such as mercury, lead, or salt.
Under-sink systems take hours to install and return about one gallon for every four gallons put in.
A semi-permeable membrane under high pressure removes particles such as bacteria, viruses, and lead and yields pure water.
Water passes four filters and, before the fourth, recycles to the refill tank and through again, reaching about 80 percent efficiency, about four times traditional reverse osmosis.
A smartphone connects to the purifier over Wi-Fi so the user can control it, see the TDS level, and share it.
Water from the purifier costs about three cents, compared with about sixty cents for Dasani, about twenty times better than typical bottled brands.
New technology creates online risks for children, and a parent's only options, reading the phone or spot-checking with saved passwords, take away the child's independence and the parent's time.
Machine-learning algorithms built from public social data and users' messages detect cyberbullying, sexting, signs of depression, or suicide.
When an issue is detected, the parent gets an alert and recommended actions, and sees only potential problems rather than every message.
The service costs $9 per month per family, with unlimited children and unlimited connected accounts.
Schools and nonprofits receive affiliate revenue for offering the service, which supports their fundraising and keeps students safer online.

A misread medical image can seriously harm a patient, radiologists face a much larger scan volume without a matching gain in reading efficiency, and training more radiologists takes a lot of time and money.
Natural language processing of medical records is paired with the imaging to give the doctor an advantage in the diagnosis.
The software is integrated into radiologists' existing workflow through vendors that already make software in this space, so doctors are not asked to adopt an unfamiliar tool.
Hospital partnerships provide the technology in exchange for medical images on which to train.
A second channel is direct sales to hospitals.
In high-inflation countries such as Argentina, Brazil, and Venezuela, most people are unbanked and lack credit, so they cannot pay online in the usual way, on credit.
The backend uses machine learning on the user's information, social data, external sources, and fraud checks to build a score that can approve credit.
Users can pay online in local-currency installments at the company's merchants and at merchants worldwide that accept Bitcoin.
Borrowers get a monthly statement and can pay it from a bank account or in cash at partner merchant locations.

Google fails to index a large share of valuable pages, about 35 percent of e-commerce pages, 45 percent of travel pages, and 55 percent of classified pages, and an ignored page cannot drive traffic or revenue.
Web crawling and log-file analysis give marketers control over how Google understands their websites.
The product is offered to businesses as a monthly SaaS subscription.
Connected home devices are easy to hack because their makers lack security knowledge, and once an attacker is on the network they can reach the other computers, files, and medical information.
A gateway sends network metadata to the cloud, where threat intelligence and machine-learning behavior models block only the behavior a device should not be doing, so the device keeps working.
When one unit blocks a threat, the other units are updated in real time so they can block that same threat.
The device costs $99 plus $8.99 a month to protect every device on the network at a business level of security.
Source code is proprietary information, intellectual property, proprietary algorithms, and the workflow of the application that runs the business.
Encryption makes data unsearchable and unusable, so core software functions become impossible and enterprises must choose between convenience and security.
Searchable encryption can search encrypted data as easily and quickly as Google without revealing the key, and it is secured with AES-256.
Encrypted Git hosting uses the same Git workflow and can migrate an existing repository in one command, encrypting the code and its history.
Transcranial direct current stimulation can stimulate the brain non-invasively, so neurostimulation can be made accessible without surgery.
Priming the motor cortex makes it more plastic, so athletes get more strength and skill from the same training.
Halo Sport is a headphone-style headset with a custom electronics board and proprietary primer electrodes, paired to an app that turns stimulation on during a workout.
The headset technology is defensible, with 27 patents filed.
Neurostimulation can help the half of stroke survivors who have a motor disability.
The company is a hardware business that makes money by selling headsets.
Primers and earpads are semi-disposable replacement parts.
The app is free for now, and premium features can be charged for later.
A large audience treats stand-up comedy as a top interest, and leading comedians reach hundreds of millions of followers.
Streaming still carries only a small share of available comedy, leaving fans without the albums people used to buy.
Transcribing every joke supports a profanity filter and radio stations built from the subject of the joke.
Listening is ad-supported, and a monthly subscription of seven dollars and ninety-nine cents adds ad-free play, offline play, and exclusive content.
Comedians promote the app because they share revenue on every stream.
The company is a primary distribution arm for the top record labels.
Cyclists and pedestrians are killed on U.S. streets at a high rate.
High-visibility clothing, retro-reflectives, and tail lights are functionally limited and often invisible from outside angles, and traditional safety vests look like traffic cones.
Electronics integrated into clothing make the wearer visible at night, and the garments are meant to look good and transition from day to night.
The software tracks the route and automatically signals turns, strobes in intersections, and flashes a brake light so drivers can see where the rider is going.
Pace lighting coaches the wearer against a target speed.
The first products are their own four-piece line for run, bike, and moto.
Parents will be able to buy the gear at college bookstores across the U.S.
Licensing places the technology with other brands in further consumer, industrial, and enterprise safety markets.
A partnership will bring a smart bike helmet to market.
Most turnover comes from soft-skill mismatch rather than hard skills, but hiring still measures resume facts such as years of experience.
Cognitive assessments are the most accurate predictors of job performance, ahead of interviews, work experience, and education.
Companies do not use those assessments because they are long, grueling, expensive, and can take days or weeks to return results.
Science-based mobile games distill traits from in-game behavior and, after 20 minutes, produce a cognitive fingerprint.
A predictive model built from a company's top performers identifies other people on the platform likely to perform like them, using demonstrated predictors rather than gender, education, or race.
Companies pay a one-time setup fee to create that predictive model from their top performers.
Companies pay a subscription to filter inbound candidates against the model.
Companies pay a sourcing fee to bring undiscovered talent from elsewhere on the platform.
Anyone can download the games for free and play them to learn their own talents.
Structural failures are the main cause of fish escapes, so submerged mooring lines and nets need daily inspection.
Farm managers' only option is commercial divers, who are expensive, must dive in pairs, and leave imprecise paper notes that have to be transcribed for regulators.

C-Drone is a portable, easy-to-pilot and easy-to-maintain underwater robot with replaceable thrusters and a wide-angle gimbal camera, it holds position in strong currents, reaches about 100 meters, and costs a fraction of existing solutions.
Inspection photos, video, and comments are stored against each structure, uploaded to a cloud service, and the farm manager can review the farm and file the report in one click.
A developer edition lets researchers hack the underwater robot, separate from the basic robot and the inspection subscription.
Single-serve pod systems are unsustainable because they create waste, the pods are expensive, and the grounds are months old, so the coffee is not fresh.
Centrifugal-force brewing manages the elements baristas and roasters use, makes styles from espresso to filter coffee, and uses no pods, filters, or other wasteful materials.
The centrifugal brewing method is patented.
When beans run low, a sensor orders replenishment from local roasters, who receive shipping and payment details and send the beans.
The app is a remote control for the machine.
They manufacture the machines and make margins on them.
They take a cut of every bean order that goes through the marketplace.
Digital tools available for under $5,000 cannot cut hard, flat materials, so those parts are still cut by hand.
Industrial waterjets that can cut those materials cost over $100,000.
A desktop waterjet cuts any material with digital precision, is more accurate than cutting by hand, and is compact, contained, clean, safe, and quiet, at a price under $4,000.
Four patents are pending on the redesigned water-cutting technology.
Relapse is driven by lack of communication and by lack of accountability for recovery activities.

The app turns a treatment plan into a schedule of sponsors, therapists, coaches, and meetings, and geolocation plus accelerometers verify that the person stayed engaged rather than checking in briefly.
A support network sees progress dashboards, gets alerts when the recovery program is missed, and can be messaged to reach out when the person starts isolating.
Rewards for active recovery are points toward fitness classes, yoga, and coffee, chosen so they do not trigger technology addiction.
The first sales channel is inpatient treatment centers in the United States.
Treatment centers receive data that helps with referrals, outcomes, and studies.
Joining huge tables on an enterprise database can take many hours.
Turning tables into matrices and distributing SQL across thousands of GPU cores makes those queries far faster than running them on CPUs.
It self-configures to the hardware in the cluster, the data stored, and the team's usage patterns.
The interface is SQL so analysts, developers, and businesses can use it, because businesses live in SQL and spend far more on SQL than on NoSQL.
The server software can be deployed on the cloud or on an on-premise rig with the appropriate configuration.
A community edition of the GPU SQL database is free to use for life.
Interfaces let users connect their own code and workbenches to the database.
Farms depend on heavily regulated H2A seasonal labor, so they must track workers and places to stay compliant, but most still use pen and paper and Department of Labor audits often find violations.
A real-time dashboard, a field tablet with NFC clock-in, and a phone app that geotags clock-ins digitize who is working, when, and where.
The system calculates the higher of hourly pay and piece-rate pay, including the added factors that make that comparison cumbersome, so payroll is accurate for labor-law compliance.
A site can recommend only from actions on its own website or app, and those actions are not placed in time, so a gift bought weeks ago is treated as the shopper's own current intent.
People keep many online identities, so their behavior sits in silos and a single website or app cannot personalize.
Brainify ties profiles from across the web to each profile's behavior and builds one encrypted, up-to-date picture of the person.
The engine assigns time-based weights and relationships to activities and, from the timeline beyond a single site, predicts what that person wants right now.
When a shopper arrives, the site calls the API and receives, in real time and in its own format, the best products for that person at that moment.
Pricing is tiered by the monthly volume of API calls so that any company can afford the service.
A hospital is mostly an administrative layer for registration, billing, and shared medical records, and most of that layer can be replaced with technology.
Scanning an insurance card pulls the carrier's information, and an emergency contact, a primary doctor, and a privacy signature finish registration without a long form.

The phone holds a condition-by-condition health record, including images, labs, referrals, and appointments, and the patient can act from it by sending prescriptions, rescheduling, viewing images, sending referrals, adding vitals, and comparing imaging prices.
Each case keeps the message history with the doctor and shows the chart the doctors use, and the doctor experience is designed along with the patient experience.
Automated questions adjust to the medical history and the answers given, a physician reviews the case, and the result is a home treatment plan or a clinic appointment.
Virtual and in-person care share context, so the clinic doctor has the virtual encounter and the patient can follow up virtually after the visit.
The system will be available to independent practices across the country.
Eight at-home kits test well-evidenced markers, from food sensitivity through women's hormones and fertility, in blood, saliva, or urine, and the current infrastructure can expand past 100 tests.
Results show specific levels and a suggested plan the customer can follow, the customer chooses how to share them, and the company does not share the data.
The service complies with direct-to-consumer testing regulations in the 46 states where it operates.
Partner labs are CLIA-certified reference laboratories that run independent validation testing.
The tests are as accurate as a test a doctor would order.
A custom platform has a virtual physician authorize the lab requisition, fulfills the kit, coordinates logistics across partner labs, and translates unstandardized HL7 into the results dashboard.
Kits sold online from $79 to $399 cost less per test than typical out-of-pocket prices and are often the same as or lower than insurance.

Custom currency is hard because payment systems do not track every code and interaction, control who can spend it and when, or tie promotions to gift cards and refunds, so firms end up building it themselves.
A web application and API let a business create, distribute, and manage its own custom currency, accept it at checkout, and give marketing control, sending, and tracking.
The service starts at $90 a month for 1,000 active codes and $15 a month per additional 1,000, so businesses of any size can use it.
Warehouse inventory tracking is manual, slow, and inaccurate, so goods are lost, workers spend hours searching, and companies lose billions to the errors.
The system is built for high-bay selective-rack warehouses with uniform dimensions, palletized goods, and a label on each pallet.

The robots fly autonomously indoors to centimeter accuracy with no external systems such as GPS, using computer vision and specialized computing hardware, and they are used to count warehouse inventory.
On-site infrastructure relays what the robots collect to the workers.
When a scan finds a discrepancy, the software tells the worker how to update SAP or fix the item in the warehouse.
Hardware is sold like traditional industrial automation equipment, for an upfront setup fee that covers the hardware and installation.

Screen installs in three commands, the same way as any other application dependency.
