Merchants pay per transaction, with no annual contract and no monthly minimum.
A proprietary neural algorithmic learning model, grounded in developmental science and cognitive neuroscience, reinforces skill sets that matter.
As children play, the system tracks skill data and recommends games and offline activities that personalize learning.
A cloning and remote-coaching system lets parents, educators, and extended family enter the game, give progressive hints, and collaborate inside a closed social network.
Parents can invite an experts and mentors network to coach inside the game and can share skill data to target development.
Outside developers can build games on the open platform's neural learning model so the games have a scientific basis for skill development.
Carriers, business phone systems, and developer telecom services have not been available together from one system of APIs.
A personal cell phone used for work lacks business-phone features such as extension dialing, call recording, and time-of-day routing.

Integrating the mobile line with the switch on the carrier network routes each cell call through the switch on a phone channel, which is what brings business features such as bring-your-own-device activation, transfer, presence, location without GPS, recording, and live transcription onto the mobile.
The same network can be deployed as a private telecom network for organizations that need isolation, including government, the military, hospitals, and banks.
International calls are much cheaper because they go through the switch via IP.
Email does not meet mobile teams that need to share files, talk, and schedule together.
Zula gives a team a structured messaging stream.
Team members can share files in the conversation and review them there, including files integrated from Dropbox and Google Drive.
A post can include a dynamic poll that shows how the team voted.
A team member can create a calendar event in the stream and the whole team receives it through calendar integration.
People can be invited from existing contacts and social networks and open that conversation directly through a deep link.
One tap starts a conference call with the people in the stream, with no phone numbers, and the call can be kept and recorded.
Consumer wearables are motivators rather than professional sport tools, and GPS is not precise enough, with an inaccuracy of about 15 feet.

QUASP tracks more than one point on the body in real time by fusing device motion readings at an access point and correcting satellite signals with differential GNSS, giving inch-accurate position, acceleration, and speed.
APIs expose acceleration, position, and speed so the platform can also be used in fields such as gaming, quadcopters, and animation.
Team sports have no technology for real-time tactical analysis, injury prevention, or talent scouting.
Patents on sensor networks and on indoor and outdoor positioning give the company a competitive advantage in that team-sport market.
Most men still shop for clothes offline because they do not know where to start online and do not trust that clothes will fit unless they try them on.
A marketplace can connect men who hate shopping with people who love to shop, because shopping for clothes is personal and requires a human touch.
Mail collects what a man likes and does not like to wear, his sizes, and his style, so shoppers can be matched to him and can improve recommendations from that profile.
Fit is sold through a pickup return service, Return Like a Man, so a man can try sizes without repackaging or a post office and is then charged only for the items he keeps plus a tip to his shopper.
People with a sense of style and time to shop, including underemployed workers who need not be fashion experts, will make money by shopping for men.
Teams at companies with large compute workloads spend months deploying software and tools so hundreds or thousands of cloud instances can work together.
Text input efficiency has gone down over the last couple of years as people type on tablets.
Drift uses the touch sensor and the accelerometer together to distinguish a tap from a resting finger, because typing thumps the screen.
Drift is for people who can type without looking, including two-finger and four-finger typists, not only ten-finger typists.
Drift will also be embedded in applications so developers can put this keyboard in an app.
Using music online increases spending, increases time in the venue, and improves perception of the brand.
Using music online is a legal nightmare, from which lawyer to hire to which copyright agencies to pay and the internet radio statute.
Analytics and A/B test infrastructure let a customer determine whether music lifts engagement, retention, and revenue.
A self-service plan provides that popular-music streaming for $25 per month.
Post-production is slowed by email threads, meetings, calls across time zones, and spreadsheets, and one minute of finished reality television can take up to 17 hours of post-production.
A viewing room keeps the focus on the video and collects timestamped comments, replies, and hotkey quick comments, pausing playback while someone types.
A review digest turns stakeholder comments into edits that can be assigned to an editor, who then gets a notification.
Comments can be exported directly into the editor's video editing software, including Adobe Premiere, and the product supports all of them.
The product is browser-based and uses existing hosting infrastructure, so IT does not have to deploy anything.
Project-based pricing is meant to be affordable for small teams while keeping upside for larger clients.
By the next update the product is meant to meet Motion Picture Association of America standards and guidelines.
Current 3D model solutions are too difficult, too expensive, or too slow for homeowners, and they are commercial tools that almost no homeowners use.
In that model a shopper can place retailer catalog furniture and personal pieces, measure the room, rearrange collections, and share the model with a designer.
The business connects retailers with homeowners because the in-home experience makes the retailer more money.
Engineers lose time because development environments do not match production, tests take too long, and a build break blocks the whole team.
Each pushed change is held in a limbo state that isolates it from the rest of the team, so a breaking change does not break the build.
Each change is tested on replicas of that engineer's production environment, on a cloud the team chooses, including behind the firewall.
The automation test suite is chunked and run in parallel across those replicas, so engineers do not wait on tests.
Customer service calls make people wait on hold and spell their name and address, including all over again after a disconnect, because the phone is a poor tool for exchanging information.
Because exchanging information in advance saves the business money, priority routing lets the caller skip the hold line.
A caller can store billing information and release it from a secure server to a payment gateway with a four-digit billing PIN instead of reading a card aloud.
Profiles are sold for 10 cents, which the pitch presents as savings of over 90 percent versus manual identification.
Partnerships with the major telephone companies supply caller information, so identification works even when the caller does not sign up.
Play is now digital and isolating, and the interactions happen through devices rather than face to face with physical objects.
A simple iPad accessory and local AI recognize ordinary physical pieces in real time, with no markers, no calibration, no network, and under any background or lighting.
The business sells physical games that come with an iPad app, with the base targeted under $30 and the games between $15 and $30.

COTA can deliver one watt at a 30-foot distance to multiple devices across a home, safely and without line of sight, because a receiver beacon leads the charger to return power only along open paths, avoiding people and anything else that absorbs energy.
COTA is in the final stages of FCC certification.
Oil and gas operations can use wireless power to eliminate the risk of sparking from wires that power their sensors.
Government policies are still communicated as unstructured text, so the public does not engage with changes that affect income by about $4,000 a year and that remain barely understood or influenced.
Millions of tax returns and census records can be merged into a model of the U.S. economy in which people configure government policies and see projected impacts on real people.
A person's endorsement is recorded in government analytics so governments can shape policies around what people want.
Government tools can already show this policy information, but they are inaccessible to the public.
A turnkey simulator can replace consulting systems that cost states between $20 million and $1.6 billion and mid-sized cities about a quarter million, saving governments money.
When money is sent home, recipients must bus to an agency, wait two hours, go to another agency to pay utility bills, and Western Union takes up to 10 percent.
Immigrants can send a credit directly to a family's cell phone in Latin America to pay for food, medicine, utility bills, and tuition.
A recipient can transfer part of the credit to family or friends, and that transfer is the basis of a social network on the remittance experience.
Customers can send online or at one of 200 partner mom-and-pop stores.
Existing contracts for 7,200 retail locations in eight countries are what allow the service to scale quickly.
Retailers pay a fee that subsidizes the price charged to sending customers.
Customers pay a low flat fee of three dollars, up to 70 percent cheaper than alternatives.
Logging in requires finding the right token or app code, and the code often changes before it can be typed.
Each login session puts a unique key in an audio signal from the computer, and the phone can receive that key only when it is close enough to confirm the session.
Proximity to the phone can replace the whole login, including username and password, as in a corporate VPN.
The login runs in the browser, supports existing computers and phones, needs no new hardware for users or the data center, and is therefore simple to set up.
An organization can limit logins and large transactions to marked places, such as home or office, and block other areas.
Understanding brain health and emotional wellbeing matters more than measuring steps and sleep.
Personality, cognition, emotion, physical health, and relationships influence daily behavior, and Tidepool works with all five.
Tidepool integrates with biometric devices such as Fitbit to give a holistic view of health.
Tidepool recommends activities based on the user's current attention and speed.
A premium model gives access to additional games and reports.
Reports can be shared with family, doctors, or coaches.
Everyday language barriers, including work and doctor visits, are not solved by machine translation or algorithms.
The current product provides live, real-time video interpretation for conferences.
Interpreters enter language, level, dialect, and accent so a user is connected to a real-time interpreter who matches.
Interpreters set weekly availability, are offered requests only during that time, and accept or decline them by push notification on a phone or laptop.
Interpreter expertise is collected so a user can be connected to someone who can handle specialized language, such as medical terms.
Professional interpreters are recruited so the service can offer a premium professional tier.

Crowdsourced interpreters are recruited across languages, trained on existing video, rated by professionals, and moved through trainee, experienced, and professional tiers so coverage can extend past major language pairs.

A minority of customers drives about half of a local business's revenue, but punch cards and mobile loyalty apps take too much effort and do not personalize offers to spending, interests, or identity.
Customers add their credit cards and earn points instantly by paying as usual, without a punch card, a phone at the register, or NFC.
Merchants can offer tailored perks, from buy-five-get-one or a percent off to exclusive access, competitions, and passes such as skipping the line.
A customer redeems a perk by presenting a virtual receipt, and the business needs no new software or hardware.
Cardify is a real-time view of who is in the store, with photo, social-media presence, and spending, functioning as a CRM for the business.
Businesses get real-time insight into how Cardify affects their bottom line and can read their customer base across multiple metrics.
Partnerships with Citigrid Media and Urban Spoon distribute Cardify to about half a million U.S. merchants.
Metals in current batteries are toxic and scarce, so recycling is only a short-term fix if the shift from fossil energy is going to scale.

Rechargeable cells use hydrogen-reinforced cellulose paper with zinc and manganese, and that material is fully compostable within a month, can be bent and cut while operating without a fire or an overheat, and is about ten times cheaper to make because the materials are abundant.
The cells are made with existing manufacturing processes and equipment.
A specialized version that increases capacity and reduces volume is for energy storage systems.
A specialized version that reduces weight and volume is for consumer tech, wearables, and remote sensors.
A specialized version that reduces weight and increases capacity is for green batteries in electric vehicles.
The hardware has gotten sturdier and more reliable.
An interchangeable dock can be swapped for an iPhone 5 version or for other handsets.
Beyond a learning tool, the device is an instrument that plays through many guitar-compatible apps, with different apps representing different parts.
In Brooklyn, about half of traffic is caused by drivers circling for a parking spot.
A driver who is leaving can offer a spot, and a driver who has never met them can find and reserve it.
Reserving a spot costs two karma credits purchased at one dollar each; the driver who gives up the spot earns one credit and Curb Karma keeps the other.
A mesh networking app lets people share mobile internet across a phone, tablet, and laptop by crowdsourcing connectivity.
The app runs on Android, Mac, and Windows laptops.
People buy brand-name clothes because they want to talk about those brands and have others know what they wear.
People can tag brands on their photos and on photos from social networks such as Facebook.
Users can ask what items are shown in photos and where to buy them.
A user can photograph an outfit, open a poll, and quickly get advice from friends and fashion experts.
Users can create wardrobes and wishlists.
A browser bookmarklet lets people tag brands on websites outside the web service.
Brands will pay to communicate with their own fans and with fans of competitors.
A marketplace in the branding area takes store price lists and automatically attaches their links by matching keywords.
